entries.section: (1) Greeting

paragraphs.text: The Apostle begins his discourse by presenting himself as an apostle of Jesus Christ by the call and will of God. He did not appoint himself an apostle, as those who opposed him in Corinth claimed. He also sends them the greeting of Sosthenes, whom he regards as his brother, who had formerly been a ruler of a synagogue of the Jews and then became a Christian.

entries.section: (1) Greeting

paragraphs.text: By calling them the Church of God, he reveals that the Church is possessed by the Lord. As for naming churches after the saints, this is to honor them and to distinguish the churches from one another because of their number. He calls them sanctified in Christ Jesus, set apart from the Gentiles and dedicated to God. That is, the Lord chose us Christians to be His own and to be called by His name.

entries.section: (1) Greeting

paragraphs.text: Finally, he grants them the apostolic blessing, which is grace, that is, the gift of God, and peace as the fruit of grace.

If you pray and call upon the name of Christ, be confident that you receive grace and peace. So take care to begin your day and end it with prayer, to take refuge in God in every affliction and to thank Him for all His gifts; for as much as your day is filled with prayer, your heart is filled with peace.

entries.section: (2) Steadfastness in the faith and readiness

paragraphs.text: The Apostle thanks God for the gifts He gave to the believers of Corinth, like the rest of the believers, which were given to them through their union with Jesus Christ, so that they became rich in the understanding of the message of the Gospel. They also stood firm in the faith in the salvation that Christ accomplished and that the Apostles preached to them, and they remained steadfast in their faith by enduring persecutions and torments even to the point of martyrdom.

entries.section: (2) Steadfastness in the faith and readiness

paragraphs.text: Their church is filled with spiritual gifts, which help in its edification and its readiness for the second coming of Christ.

entries.section: (2) Steadfastness in the faith and readiness

paragraphs.text: The Lord Jesus Christ will confirm them in the faith to the end of their life on earth, so that there will be nothing in them for which they could be blamed on the day of judgment.

entries.section: (2) Steadfastness in the faith and readiness

paragraphs.text: God is faithful in His call to them, for He will bring them into the life of fellowship in His Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

Looking to the heavenly Kingdom makes you hold fast to your faith, your prayers and your church, and bind yourself to your fellow believers. Thus you grow in the love of God and make light of the desires of the world, and also of its cares and toils; rather, you experience the love of God every day and long to be with Him.

entries.section: (3) Disputes among believers

paragraphs.text: "Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment." The Apostle calls them brethren, for all Christians, in the fellowship of the blood of Christ, have become brethren in one body, whose head is Christ and whose members are the members of the Church. So when we divide among ourselves and quarrel with one another, it is as if we were dividing the one body of Christ. How hard that is on the heart of Christ, because of the disturbance it brings to the one Church and the stumbling blocks it causes! This also shows the humility of Paul, who had the right to call them my children or my sons, for he was their bishop and their father, yet he called them brethren.

entries.section: (3) Disputes among believers

paragraphs.text: For it has been declared to me by those of the house of Chloe, a woman well known to the Christians of Corinth, that there are contentions among you which have led you into division.

entries.section: (3) Disputes among believers

paragraphs.text: Among you are those who say that they follow Paul and form factions for him; others follow Apollos, who was a Jew who became a Christian, an Alexandrian learned in the Scriptures and concerned with interpretation; a group who admired his eloquence followed him and formed factions for him. Among you are those who follow Cephas (the Jewish name of Peter) and form factions for him, and among you are those who set up a party and called themselves the party of Christ.

entries.section: (3) Disputes among believers

paragraphs.text: The Apostle affirms, in the form of questions, that Christ is one and was crucified for all, and that no one else redeemed them, not even Paul, and that they were not baptized in his name.

The word "in the name" in Greek means Christ's ownership of the one baptized and his union with Him. In the Liturgy of St. Gregory, in the first litany, the Church reminds us to pray all together, asking for oneness of heart and the ending of the divisions of the Church.
The Apostle asks the believers to have the mind of Christ, that is, one mind (ch. 2:16).

entries.section: (3) Disputes among believers

paragraphs.text: The Apostle thanks God that he baptized none of them but Crispus, who was a ruler of a Jewish synagogue and believed through the hand of the Apostle Paul, and Gaius, who was a Christian who hosted the meetings of the Church in his house, and himself Paul, so that no one should say that he had baptized in his own name. He also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, he does not mention that he baptized anyone else. The Apostle is not concerned to baptize personally, because his chief work as a bishop is preaching under the guidance of the Holy Spirit and not with the philosophy of the world.

Hold your own opinion even if it differs from others, for differing opinions complete one another; but beware of divisions, for they carry pride and lack of love. Do not oppose in order to show yourself off, but be diligent for peace and unity.

entries.section: (4) The Cross is the power and the wisdom of God

paragraphs.text: The Cross of Christ, in the eyes of unbelievers, who will perish because of their unbelief, is a kind of foolishness, because it shows the weakness of Christ. But to us, who are saved by the work of the Cross, it is the power of God, which transfers us from the death of sin to life in Christ.

entries.section: (4) The Cross is the power and the wisdom of God

paragraphs.text: It is written (in Isa 29:14) that by the divine wisdom, in accomplishing salvation by the Cross, the Lord made void all the human wisdom of the wise, which was unable to set man right; therefore the Church took the Cross as a symbol of salvation.

entries.section: (4) The Cross is the power and the wisdom of God

paragraphs.text: The Apostle asks a rhetorical question in order to expose the failure of the Jews and the philosophers of the Gentiles, with all their wisdom, knowledge and ability to debate, to repair the corruption that had befallen man.

entries.section: (4) The Cross is the power and the wisdom of God

paragraphs.text: The world could not know God through His wisdom, which is clearly declared in all creation, so He was pleased to save them from sin by what He accomplished by His death on the Cross, which unbelievers regard as foolishness.

entries.section: (4) The Cross is the power and the wisdom of God

paragraphs.text: For the Jews seek a mighty, powerful savior who does miraculous works, and the Greeks seek a savior marked by philosophy and wisdom. Therefore our preaching of Christ crucified is not accepted by the Jews, who were awaiting salvation from the Romans and not from sin, and it contradicts the wisdom of the Greeks, who regard the preaching of the Cross as foolishness.

entries.section: (4) The Cross is the power and the wisdom of God

paragraphs.text: As for us believers, whether we are Jews or Greeks, we have recognized the power of God and the wisdom of God in accomplishing salvation by the Cross.

entries.section: (4) The Cross is the power and the wisdom of God

paragraphs.text: What seems to others to be foolishness has accomplished for mankind what their wisdom was unable to accomplish, and what seems to be weakness in the Cross has accomplished the salvation that all human powers were unable to accomplish.
Receive the word of God with faith and submission so that you may apply it in your life and it may work in you, and reject doubts or any thought that is not edifying, however logical it may appear.

entries.section: (5) Boasting in the Lord

paragraphs.text: "For ye see your calling, brethren": consider the Lord's call to you, that it was not based on any human wisdom you had, or the power of your social standing, or your family and lineage, as proved by the fact that there are not many among you who have wisdom, or power, or nobility of birth.

entries.section: (5) Boasting in the Lord

paragraphs.text: God chose the simple, whom people regard as weak and ignorant, yet His work appeared clearly in their lives by their acceptance of the salvation which others, wise in their own eyes, were unable to understand.

entries.section: (5) Boasting in the Lord

paragraphs.text: God also chose those who are weak in their standing and lineage, and "base things", that is, those who are not of the upper class in society, and "things which are despised", that is, those held in contempt in the eyes of people, and "things which are not", that is, those who have no account among people, in order to bring to nothing, by their salvation, the arguments of all the prominent in society. This was made clear in the Lord's choice of His disciples and apostles, most of whom were from the simple class in society.

entries.section: (5) Boasting in the Lord

paragraphs.text: This is so that those who have human power or wisdom may be certain that salvation does not come by power or wisdom.

entries.section: (5) Boasting in the Lord

paragraphs.text: "Of Him are ye in Christ Jesus": it is from Christ that your call came, to life with Him and to receiving wisdom, righteousness and sanctification.

entries.section: (5) Boasting in the Lord

paragraphs.text: So let our boasting be in the Lord, for all our abilities are a gift from Him, and by this we are saved from pride.
God is ready to work through you however weak you may be. So trust in His power and seek the salvation of those around you; and as much as you thank God, His grace increases in you.
The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. Spiritual wisdom

entries.section: (1) Preaching with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul reminds them that when he preached the Gospel to them he did not rely on eloquence and philosophy, but concentrated his speech on the story of the salvation accomplished by Jesus Christ on the Cross, whose effect on everyone who hears it surpasses in power any eloquence of expression.

Do not rely, in persuading others, on your philosophy and your own abilities, but through prayer receive grace to present your words in a simple and convincing way. And if God wishes, He will guide you by using the various means of persuasion, so that your reliance is on God in everything.

entries.section: (1) Preaching with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul means that he did not preach Christ relying on any human ability or power; on the contrary, his sense of the weight of the responsibility put him in a state of great fear.

entries.section: (1) Preaching with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: Likewise he did not preach to them relying on human wisdom and rhetorical, rational persuasion, but relied on the powerful guidance of the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (1) Preaching with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: This was so that all might know that the credit for their faith does not belong to rational proofs, but to the divine power that is able to establish them in the faith.

It is good that you appreciate the weight of the responsibility upon you, and pray, asking for God's help, and carry out the work with care because you are liable to error, and accept the guidance of others and their completing of what you do.

entries.section: (1) Preaching with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul goes on to say that he speaks among those who are spiritually mature a wisdom that is not of this world, that is, not an invention of men or of the great ones of the world, whose destiny is to come to an end.

entries.section: (1) Preaching with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: Paul speaks the wisdom of God which He declared in the Gospel, which is like a mystery to unbelievers. The mystery here is everything that was declared in the Gospel concerning the matters of redemption by Jesus Christ, for they cannot grasp it, because it is the wisdom hidden from the human mind; although God prepared it from eternity, He did not declare it until this age, so that we might have a share in eternal glory.

entries.section: (1) Preaching with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The great ones of the world cannot attain this wisdom, for had they known that Christ is the Son of God, they would not have dared to crucify Him.

So we Christians must not boast of our earthly wisdom, but rather strive to be filled with the divine wisdom which the Holy Spirit gives us, as the Apostle James said, that if we ever have bitter envying and strife in our hearts, we should know that this wisdom does not descend from above.

entries.section: (2) The work of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: Here the Apostle speaks of the eternal glory that God has prepared for us, which surpasses everything our senses can grasp. No one can imagine it, and no human being has ever seen it or heard of it. So we too must choose between the spiritual perfection that leads us to eternal glory, and vain greatness that causes envy and strife.

entries.section: (2) The work of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: By the Spirit we can sense the majesty of this glory through what God reveals to us by His Holy Spirit, who knows all that is God's.

entries.section: (2) The work of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: To clarify this idea, the Apostle sets man before us as an example. Just as the spirit of man knows his intentions and the thoughts of his heart, so also the Spirit of God knows all the things of God and declares them to us.

entries.section: (2) The work of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The spiritual things that are revealed by the Holy Spirit we know from the Holy Spirit who dwells in us, which is impossible for the people of the world, in whom the Spirit of God does not dwell. For we, by Baptism and the Holy Myron, have had the Holy Spirit descend upon us, and have become qualified to receive the gifts and fruits of the Holy Spirit.
So let us take care not to "quench the Spirit", but practice the spiritual means so that we may grow in the Spirit.

entries.section: (2) The work of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: The Apostle goes on to say: We too, when we speak of these things in our preaching, do not use human wisdom to convey their meanings to people, but draw wisdom from the Holy Spirit who dwells in us, and so use spiritual expressions to present spiritual concepts. It is not right that spiritual things be judged by earthly, temporal measures and standards.

The Holy Spirit who dwells in you is able to search the depths of God. How great are these blessings, because through them you can grow in your prayers and enjoy communion with God, and also understand and delight in His word in the Holy Bible. For God wants to bring you into His embrace, that you may be united with Him and rejoice in being always with Him. So ask for the help of the Holy Spirit in all your spiritual practices, and you will be filled with vitality and a sense of God.

entries.section: (3) The mind of the spiritual man

paragraphs.text: The natural man, who is the man who lives in material things and judges matters by a material measure, finds it impossible to accept spiritual things; indeed, the teachings of the Holy Spirit are considered by him wrong and unsound, because knowing these things requires a spiritual knowledge entirely higher than the limits of his human knowledge.

entries.section: (3) The mind of the spiritual man

paragraphs.text: The spiritual man has, beyond his material abilities, spiritual abilities, which he receives from the Holy Spirit who dwells in him, so that he is able to discern not only fleshly matters but spiritual ones as well. Therefore it is not the right of the man who has only human abilities to judge the spiritual man; for how can he judge spiritual matters that do not at all fall within the scope of his fleshly knowledge? On the contrary, the spiritual man easily discerns and judges all those around him.
The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

entries.section: (3) The mind of the spiritual man

paragraphs.text: He who knows the mind of the Lord is able to teach it to others and to judge among them on the basis of this mind. Therefore the natural man, who does not know the mind of Christ, has no right to teach us and to judge us, who in fact have the mind of Christ.

To have the mind of Christ means to see things as Christ sees them and to measure them by the measure by which Christ measures. So the Apostle wants to say that the judgment of the philosophers that my teaching is ignorance is a false judgment that carries no weight.

Do not be disturbed by the objections of those far from the Church to your spiritual conduct, but stand firm in your life with God, submissive to the guidance of your father of confession and your spiritual guides, and ask for the guidance of the Holy Spirit to understand the right conduct with all those around you.
The servant, the ministry and salvation

entries.section: (1) The carnal man

paragraphs.text: The Apostle cannot speak to them as people who have matured spiritually, but as beginners in the knowledge of Christ, like children with regard to the knowledge of God's wisdom and will, because they are still occupied with fleshly, that is, material, things.

entries.section: (1) The carnal man

paragraphs.text: Just as milk is given to children because they have no ability to digest the food of adults, so the Apostle Paul spoke to them, as spiritual beginners, only of the basics of Christianity, because they had not yet acquired the ability to enter into the depth of spiritual knowledge.

entries.section: (1) The carnal man

paragraphs.text: Envy is caused by distorted passions, strife is caused by arguments born of pride and self, and division is the practical behavior that follows from these. The proof that the description of the carnal man applies to them is the presence of envy, strife and factions among them, which are the marks of those who walk according to the desires of the flesh, so that their conduct is equal to the conduct of those who have not yet accepted the faith.

Let us look within ourselves to see how far our sensual desires affect our lives. Do we envy others for the material things they own and we do not? Do we quarrel with one another? If so, let us understand that we are still short of the spirituality that the children of the Kingdom must have, that spirituality which is the true goal that every Christian seeks, and which is achieved only when our desires are united with the will of God.

entries.section: (1) The carnal man

paragraphs.text: In a question of astonishment, he affirms the carnal level by which they live, when some of them form factions by following Paul and others Apollos; their inner motives are still not for Christ.

entries.section: (2) The work of God and the work of the servant

paragraphs.text: By his question, "Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos?", the Apostle Paul draws the attention of the people of Corinth to the fact that Paul and Apollos are no more than servants of the Lord, whom He used as a means to deliver His message to them, by the gifts and abilities that the Lord gave to each of them to help them deliver the message.

entries.section: (2) The work of God and the work of the servant

paragraphs.text: Here the Apostle likens them to a field in which Paul cast the seed of spiritual knowledge that leads to salvation, through his preaching, and then Apollos watered this seed through his spiritual teachings; but the more important work is the work of the Lord, who makes this seed grow, and without His work the harvest cannot be gathered.

entries.section: (2) The work of God and the work of the servant

paragraphs.text: But Paul and Apollos do not possess the power of making grow, which God alone possesses, and without it the casting of the seed and the watering of it have no result. This does not cancel the work of the servants, but makes clear that success is by the work of God.

entries.section: (2) The work of God and the work of the servant

paragraphs.text: He who casts the seed or waters it performs a part of one work; therefore this should not be a reason for separate allegiance, that is, division, for the work is one, and each of them will receive a reward from the Lord according to his diligence in the work.

entries.section: (2) The work of God and the work of the servant

paragraphs.text: Here he again likens them to a field and to a building. Paul and Apollos are each workers whom the Lord uses in tilling the field or in laying the foundation of the building, a work which the Lord accomplishes by His power and will.

If you offer service or care to someone, whether in your house for your relatives or in the Church, know that you are an instrument in the hand of God, and that He is the true Father and Shepherd. Therefore ask for His help; do not be proud or boast of what you do, or blame others for not appreciating your labor; thank God for every success that is achieved; and beware of rejoicing in praise and gathering people around you, for you are merely a servant of God, so do not steal His glory and turn it to yourself.

entries.section: (3) Spiritual edification and the evaluation of service

paragraphs.text: "According to the grace of God which is given unto me" as an apostle, I became like a wise masterbuilder, and laid the strong foundation, which is faith in Christ; but everyone who builds good works and services upon this foundation must take heed how he builds, so that his works are done from a pure heart and with faithfulness.

entries.section: (3) Spiritual edification and the evaluation of service

paragraphs.text: No one can lay another foundation in place of the one I laid as the foundation of your spiritual edification, which is faith in Jesus Christ and His Church.

entries.section: (3) Spiritual edification and the evaluation of service

paragraphs.text: Gold, silver, precious stones: heavenly spiritual services that influence those served, because gold signifies heaven, silver the word of God, and precious stones the spiritual virtues. Wood, hay, stubble: social and athletic services and activities that have no purpose or relation to spiritual things; for wood, stubble and hay are materials easily burned and destroyed, signifying all superficial services whose effect quickly comes to an end.

entries.section: (3) Spiritual edification and the evaluation of service

paragraphs.text: The fruits of the service will be evident. The servant of the first kind will have good fruit in those he serves, while the servant of the second kind will not have fruit among those he serves like the first, because his teachings were weak. This will be revealed on the day of judgment (the testing by fire, that is, the divine judgment).

entries.section: (3) Spiritual edification and the evaluation of service

paragraphs.text: If the effect of the service endures in those served and they advance spiritually, the servant will receive a reward in heaven.

entries.section: (3) Spiritual edification and the evaluation of service

paragraphs.text: If those served do not stand firm before the fires of trials and afflictions, that is, if all the labors of the servant are burned up and vanish, and those served are far from God, the servant will lose the reward of his service because it was a superficial and weak service, but he will be saved for the sake of his faith despite his failure in the service. The phrase "he shall be saved" refers to the servant whose service did not bring the desired result, but whose personal life was one of faith and good work, and the phrase "he shall suffer loss" refers to the reward for the service. This shows the importance of the servant's striving in the service, and also shows that there is recompense for works.

All the talk is about the labors of the service and their evaluation on the day of judgment: either they are of value and we receive a reward, or they are weak and are burned up, that is, become worthless. It has no relation to the servant's personal salvation, for he will be saved for the sake of his faith, but "so as by fire", that is, barely, because of the absence of good works and of a service of value before God. This does not mean that there is a fire in heaven by which the righteous are tormented before they enter Paradise, as the adherents of the heresy of purgatory claim.

entries.section: (4) The Church is the temple of God

paragraphs.text: Do you not know that you have been sanctified by your membership in the body of Christ, and have become like the Holy of Holies which belongs to the Lord, and His Holy Spirit has descended upon you and dwelt in you by the Holy Myron?

entries.section: (4) The Church is the temple of God

paragraphs.text: If any servant spreads among you the spirit of division and factionalism, he thereby tears the one body, that is, the body of Christ, which is the Church, and this servant will be deprived of the work of the Holy Spirit in him, and his salvation will become difficult.

This shows that we as believers do not belong to ourselves but to God. Likewise, whoever insists on defiling his senses and corrupting them by sin wrongs his body, which belongs to God; and our God is just, so He will punish him with destruction and eternal corruption, in addition to the fact that a person is often exposed to diseases that strike his body as a result of falling into sins that harm his body, such as fornication and anger.
Keep your senses pure and flee from evil so that you may enjoy a pure body, for it is the temple of God; and if you corrupt it by any sin, hasten to repentance to restore its purity.

entries.section: (5) Divine wisdom

paragraphs.text: Let no man deceive himself into thinking that he is wise because of his distinction in intelligence and understanding; by this pride he harms himself and may cause problems and divisions in the Church. He must humble himself before God as a fool, that he may learn spiritual wisdom from Him.

entries.section: (5) Divine wisdom

paragraphs.text: The wisdom of this world, which cannot understand the truth of this salvation and redemption accomplished on the Cross, is foolishness itself with God. For it is written that their refusal to accept the true wisdom will in the end lead to the destruction of their souls, so that everyone will see that their earthly wisdom did not achieve salvation for them.

entries.section: (5) Divine wisdom

paragraphs.text: Also God knows that earthly wisdom does not help anyone to be saved; it is vain, that is, worthless, for understanding this salvation.

To acquire wisdom we must hold fast to our spiritual worship and all works of mercy, and walk in goodness, so that we become fit for wisdom to dwell in us; and when we acquire wisdom we increase in goodness and righteousness, and God grants us still more wisdom. Thus wisdom and goodness each cause the other to grow.

entries.section: (6) All things are yours and you are Christ's

paragraphs.text: Here the Apostle Paul returns and forbids them to follow particular persons, who become the object of their pride and of their admiration for their intellectual or oratorical abilities, because these abilities are gifts from God given to these persons for the benefit of the Church and the salvation of the souls of its members.

entries.section: (6) All things are yours and you are Christ's

paragraphs.text: All the servants, and what is in the world, and life and death, and things present and things to come, are the work of God in the servants and through them for the accomplishment of their salvation. For life, to believers, is an opportunity for communion with God and preparation for eternity, and death is a passage toward the Kingdom.

entries.section: (6) All things are yours and you are Christ's

paragraphs.text: But you are Christ's, who bought you with His precious blood, and He is the Son of the Father by nature and one with Him in essence, and He made us children of God by adoption.

Your abilities are divine gifts to you which should be used for the glory of God. So do not neglect them, for they belong to God and He will call you to account for them: did you use them only for your own benefit, or for the benefit of those around you? And what can you offer to the Church while you are heedless of it?
Remember, O Lord, Your maidservant: the humility of the servant with those served, and his firmness with them

entries.section: (1) Faithfulness in service

paragraphs.text: "Let a man so account of us", me and Apollos and the rest of the priests, as servants of Christ, not as masters over you, serving His Church, and entrusted by Him with the Holy Mysteries.

The word "mysteries" here means the truths and beliefs that are above the human mind, which man grasps only by faith, such as the seven sacraments of the Church. These truths and beliefs are necessary for the sanctification of man and his preparation for the life of fellowship with God.

entries.section: (1) Faithfulness in service

paragraphs.text: The most important quality of a steward is to be faithful in the responsibility his master entrusts to him. If this is required in worldly affairs, it is required all the more in spiritual affairs, that is, of spiritual stewards.

entries.section: (1) Faithfulness in service

paragraphs.text: If the believers of Corinth formed factions for Apollos and Cephas, preferring them to Paul, Paul does not care about their opinions concerning his faithfulness in the service, nor about any human court. He called the human court "man's day", as the divine court is called the day of judgment or the day of the Lord. For the judgments of men are not free of errors in judging matters, and they did not send him or command him to teach; he is not their steward but God's steward. Paul added that he also does not rely on any wisdom in himself, because he knows that he too is imperfect and liable to error and self-indulgence, and that the conscience of any man is not infallible, and therefore he does not judge himself.

entries.section: (1) Faithfulness in service

paragraphs.text: Although my conscience does not reproach me for any shortcoming in carrying out my apostolic duties in the service, this feeling of mine is not proof of the perfection of my faithfulness in the service and my innocence of shortcoming in the stewardship; I accept only the judgment of the Lord Jesus upon me, for He searches the hearts and knows the intentions, and nothing is hidden from Him.

entries.section: (1) Faithfulness in service

paragraphs.text: "Therefore judge nothing before the time", whether concerning me or concerning Apollos, and leave this to the day of judgment, and do not give yourselves a right that belongs to God alone, who, when He comes for judgment, will "bring to light the hidden things of darkness", that is, things hidden from sight, and will make manifest the secrets of hearts, and reveal all the works of men and all the thoughts of their hearts; and every man who was faithful inwardly as outwardly will receive from God the praise he deserves.

Would that we might benefit from this advice, so that we do not pass judgments on others but leave the judgment to the just Judge, who sees what we cannot see and examines what we cannot examine, so that His judgments are just. As for our own opinions of others, they depend on the appearances of things and do not reach the whole truth, and so they are liable to error.

entries.section: (2) Gifts are a divine gift

paragraphs.text: What I said about myself, Paul, and Apollos, as an example for servants in submission and in surrendering our lives to God, I intended so that you may learn to give glory to God, and that none of you be puffed up against another or form a faction and boast, so that divisions arise which harm the Church.

entries.section: (2) Gifts are a divine gift

paragraphs.text: Every knowledge or gift in a person is a divine gift and a distinction received as a grant from God, and he has no merit in it. How, then, can there be room for one person to boast over another, as though he had obtained this gift by himself and had not received it as a free gift from God?

Thank God for every gift or ability that you enjoy, and be faithful in using it for His glory, so that you help those around you whenever God gives you the opportunity. Learn from the fathers and spiritual servants, but do not become attached to any one of them, for they are the means through which God conveys His blessings to you. Let your heart be attached to God; do not form a faction for any teacher and keep away from, or reject, another, but learn from all, and see God in all their teachings.

entries.section: (3) The pride of the Corinthians and the endurance of the Apostles

paragraphs.text: You have been content with the blessings and spiritual knowledge you have obtained and no longer need more; you thought that you had reached the highest degrees of spiritual grace and had become perfect of yourselves, without help from us the Apostles; and beyond your fullness and self-sufficiency you thought that you had come to reign with Christ, and enjoyed the joys of the Kingdom, and reached the highest degrees of spiritual grace until you thought that you had become kings in the Kingdom of Heaven, and that you had obtained perfect holiness and gained every spiritual blessing. I wish that your illusion were truth, so that we might share with you in the glory and the blessings.

entries.section: (3) The pride of the Corinthians and the endurance of the Apostles

paragraphs.text: "A spectacle unto the world": it mocks us for the insults we endure.
"To angels and to men": the angels rejoice in us and the believers among men imitate us.

God allowed us the Apostles to be put last of all, as though sentenced to death (the Romans used to put their captives at the end of the triumphal procession); and in truth we have faced death every day for the sake of Christ, and have become a wonder to the beholders because of the severity of our afflictions, and have become an object of mockery to the world, but the object of the admiration of the angels.

entries.section: (3) The pride of the Corinthians and the endurance of the Apostles

paragraphs.text: In this verse and those that follow, the Apostle describes the poor condition of the Apostles and contrasts it with the condition of those Corinthians who imagined that they had become happy. There is clear sarcasm in this, as though he said to them: how great is the difference between us and you; you are at the highest degrees of happiness and we are at the lowest ranks of misery. He says: you consider us unworthy to teach you, and you have become wise, needing no teaching, as if you had gained wisdom by your union with Christ; but we, because of our zeal in serving Christ, are considered by you to be fools. Some accuse us of weakness, but you, in your own opinion, are strong and need the support of no one, and you reckon that you deserve honor and that we deserve contempt.

entries.section: (3) The pride of the Corinthians and the endurance of the Apostles

paragraphs.text: Even to this present hour we the Apostles endure hunger and thirst and other hardships and afflictions, and we have no dwelling place, for we are always sojourners and strangers in our journeys from place to place to preach the Gospel and to flee from the persecutors.

entries.section: (3) The pride of the Corinthians and the endurance of the Apostles

paragraphs.text: We support ourselves by the labor of our hands; Paul used to work at making tents, although he had the right that the Church should support him, as stated in (ch. 9:14), but he did not ask for this; and we repay evil with good and cursing with blessing, and we endure persecution without complaint or murmuring.

entries.section: (3) The pride of the Corinthians and the endurance of the Apostles

paragraphs.text: They ascribe bad qualities to us and we answer with gentle words, imitating Christ, who, when He was reviled, reviled not again; when He suffered, He threatened not, but committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously (1 Pet 2:23). We have come to the extreme of contempt and lowliness in the cause of serving Christ and the Church.

Do not think that you have arrived at the righteousness and the life that please God, lest you grow lazy in continuing your spiritual striving and growth in the love of God; and look to the fathers and spiritual teachers to learn from them and imitate them.

entries.section: (4) Spiritual fatherhood

paragraphs.text: I do not mean by this manner of my writing to shame you, by comparing your condition with our labors the Apostles, and by answering what you imagine of yourselves; rather I speak to you as a father who loves you, and so I warn you that you may return to what is right.

entries.section: (4) Spiritual fatherhood

paragraphs.text: Though there are many who take you by the hand to guide you in the spiritual life, you have no spiritual fathers other than me (for Paul was the means of their faith in Christ, by his proclaiming to them the Gospel, the power of God unto salvation). The father is the one who sows the seeds of faith, while the guide follows the believer and takes him by the hand. So I ask you, because I am your spiritual father and you are confident of my love for you and my desire to benefit you, to walk in my way and follow my course in offering my life to the service of Christ.
Would that we might be disciples of our spiritual fathers whom we love and trust, so that they may be an example to us in the way of life, and we may imitate them in our conduct and our spirituality.

entries.section: (5) A call to return to what is right

paragraphs.text: "For this cause", that is, that you may remember my way and my teaching, I have sent unto you Timothy, my companion in my journeys and my helper, who is worthy to act on my behalf and is faithful in the service of Christ and His Gospel, to remind you of my ways in Christ, that is, humility and faithfulness to God, and to bring to your attention my teaching, which is one in every place where I have preached.

entries.section: (5) A call to return to what is right

paragraphs.text: Some proud false teachers claimed that Paul was weak and did not dare to come to Corinth, but he paid no attention to their words and sent his disciple Timothy to confirm his teachings.

Do not be shaken by the words of the wicked who oppose the word of God and who describe you as weak and ignorant because of your clinging to God. Stand firm in the teachings of the Church and ask for God's help and wisdom.

entries.section: (5) A call to return to what is right

paragraphs.text: I will come to you shortly, if the Lord will, and I will reveal to you the disagreement between the works of these men and their words. For Christ gave the Apostles power which appeared repeatedly in miracles, in speaking with tongues, and in their ability to draw people to Christ, whereas the proud false teachers have no such power, and this is proof that God did not send them to that service.

entries.section: (5) A call to return to what is right

paragraphs.text: For true religion is not mere pretension and confession with the tongue, but a change of heart, a reform of conduct, and a life we live with God.

entries.section: (5) A call to return to what is right

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul left it to them to choose between his coming to them as one who rebukes and reproves, or as a tender comforter. That is, do they want him to come and cut some of them off from the Church as a discipline for them for their opposition and pride, or to come to them with words of forgiveness and peace if they turn away from disputes and quarrels? The authority of the Church and the problem of the fornicator

entries.section: (1) The problem of fornication and how the Apostle dealt with it

paragraphs.text: One of the believers in Corinth sinned by committing fornication with his father's wife. This sin is against sound human nature and is rare even among unbelievers, so how much more shameful is the fall of one of the believers into it!

entries.section: (1) The problem of fornication and how the Apostle dealt with it

paragraphs.text: Here the Apostle Paul returns to what he had already pointed out, the boasting of the Corinthians in their spiritual virtues, and asks: how can you claim knowledge and wisdom for yourselves, when you should rather have been ashamed when you heard that such an abomination had occurred among you? You did not rebuke yourselves and mourn for the disgrace you brought upon the Church, which ought to be pure like its Lord. Instead of being proud, you ought to have removed the one who committed this iniquity from among you.

entries.section: (1) The problem of fornication and how the Apostle dealt with it

paragraphs.text: Paul was in Ephesus when he wrote this epistle, but that did not prevent him from considering and judging the matter of the one among the members of the church of Corinth who committed this act, as though he were present among them in spirit, thinking of them, caring for their success and suffering for every harm that befell them. He had the right and the authority which he received from the Lord Jesus, and he reckoned the members of the Church to be gathered together and himself to be among them in spirit.

entries.section: (1) The problem of fornication and how the Apostle dealt with it

paragraphs.text: Paul pronounced judgment that he be cut off and deprived of the Church and of partaking of the Holy Mysteries, in the hope that he would repent when he suffered from this deprivation and became aware of the horror of his sin, and so repent; then the Church would receive him and he would regain the purity of his body and spirit, and be saved on the day of judgment.

This shows that the authority of excommunication from the Church is an apostolic tradition and a scriptural commandment, since the Apostles and the priests, their successors, have the right to this action if circumstances require it. The source of authority to cut someone off from the Church is the Lord Jesus, who declared that it is necessary, and the one who commanded that it be carried out is the Apostle Paul. This Church discipline always turns to benefit, and if the person accepts it and repents, he escapes eternal judgment.

This abominable sin did not happen suddenly but is the result of gradual negligence. So watch the beginnings of sins, such as a look, a thought or an emotional inclination, so that you do not defile yourself, for all of these are stages of fornication; and give up any of them however beloved, and keep away from whoever encourages you in it.

entries.section: (2) The necessity of purging the Church of the corrupt

paragraphs.text: You boast of your wisdom and your spiritual gifts, but this has no real basis, because your condition calls for shame and for fear of the spread of evil as a result of the error of one member of your church, whom others will imitate. To explain this, the Apostle Paul uses the idea that a small amount of leaven is able to leaven a large amount of dough, to warn them that just as one sin, if its doer does not repent, opens many doors before him to commit other sins, so sin spreads from one person to another within the community. If someone transgresses the commandments of God and is not rebuked, disciplined and set apart, others imitate him and make light of iniquity.

entries.section: (2) The necessity of purging the Church of the corrupt

paragraphs.text: It is therefore your duty to remove the person who sinned from your midst, and to cleanse yourselves and your church community of the corruption that has accompanied human nature since the Fall, so that you become pure, renewed and holy, purged of sin, as unleavened bread is free of leaven. Just as the Jews purified themselves at the Passover according to the Mosaic law, when they slaughtered the Passover lamb and went on eating unleavened bread for seven days in the feast of unleavened bread, which signifies the whole of life, so also, since Christ has been slaughtered for us and has become our Passover, we must purge ourselves of every evil.

entries.section: (2) The necessity of purging the Church of the corrupt

paragraphs.text: So let your whole life be holy to God, as a perpetual holy feast, with a pure, renewed nature and not, as before, a corrupt human nature. The corrupt nature is liable to evil and malice, but the renewed nature is a nature sincere in its purity and its good, blameless conduct, and loving all that is true. Sincerity points to holiness of conduct and behavior, and truth points to holiness of spiritual doctrine and faith.

God was sincere in His love for you and died to redeem you, and He cares for you every day. Are you sincere toward Him and do you strive to please Him? Do you refuse every evil that angers Him, and rejoice in being often with Him in prayers and readings?

entries.section: (3) The Church has the right to judge its members

paragraphs.text: I wrote to you before, in (vv. 1, 2), to keep away from fornicators. But I never meant that you should withdraw from the fornicators of this world, that is, from unbelievers, or from the covetous who desire to gain wealth by any means, whether justly or unjustly, or from extortioners, who wrong others by taking more than is their right, or from idolaters, who worship false gods. For if I had meant to forbid you to associate with such people, it would be as if I were commanding you to depart to another world than this one, because such people are found everywhere in the world, and we must deal with them in the transactions necessary for life.

entries.section: (3) The Church has the right to judge its members

paragraphs.text: And now I make clearer to you what I meant when I wrote to you before. If anyone claims to be a Christian and has entered into the fellowship of the Church but is a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler of others, or drinks wine excessively to the point of drunkenness, or wrongs others, I tell you: keep away from this person; for if he is defiled by the corruption that is in the world and the Church nevertheless keeps him in its midst, it is as if it allows the world to enter it, which makes the Church lose its spirituality and holiness and everything by which it is distinguished of truth and purity.

entries.section: (3) The Church has the right to judge its members

paragraphs.text: It is not for me or for you to judge those who are outside the Church, but those who are inside the Church.

entries.section: (3) The Church has the right to judge its members

paragraphs.text: As for those outside the Church, God alone judges them, whether in the present world or on the last day. It is your right, indeed your duty, to separate the one who walks in evil and malice among you.

Open your heart in love to every person and pray for those who are far away and for sinners, but do not mingle or associate with the wicked and become accustomed to sitting with them and amusing yourself with them, lest you be swept along into their sins. Be humble and careful, and God will keep you from sin.
Lawsuits between believers

entries.section: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

paragraphs.text: "Dare any of you, having a matter against another", such as a disagreement over dividing money, property or an inheritance, go to law before the pagans? The Apostle Paul called them "the unjust" because they violated the law of righteousness by their worship of idols and their denial of the true God, and in contrast he called the believers "saints". Through this astonished question, the Apostle Paul considered it a disgrace for Christians to be unable to settle the disputes of the brethren and to resort to pagan courts to judge between them.

entries.section: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

paragraphs.text: You know perfectly well that your conduct as believers will judge the world that did not believe. The sitting of the saints with Christ for judgment confirms that He considered them worthy to judge. If believers are worthy to judge on the day of judgment, they are all the more worthy to judge in worldly matters, those concerning money and what relates to it, which are very small matters compared with the matters of the day of judgment. This is why the Church holds to having a special law for the personal status of Christians.

entries.section: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

paragraphs.text: You also know, from Christian teaching, that you will judge the angels who fell, that is, the demons, on the day of judgment, for their refusal to submit to God (Jude 2, 6 Pet 3:4). All the more are you worthy to judge people in temporal matters.

entries.section: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

paragraphs.text: Here the Apostle's words carry the sense of astonishment and rebuke. By "those who are least esteemed" is meant those of less standing. So set them as judges among you, for the least among you understands the commandments of God better than the pagans of the world.

entries.section: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

paragraphs.text: I say this to make you ashamed of your improper conduct. It is a great disgrace for those who claim wisdom that they find no wise man among them fit to judge between the brethren (how is this, is there not a wise man among you?). Therefore they are compelled to resort to the pagan courts.

entries.section: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

paragraphs.text: How can a brother accept being taken to court by his brother over the matters of this life before pagan judges? The Holy Bible does not mean here to reject the authority of the civil courts, for it calls us to submit to the rulers and authorities of the world (Rom 13:1-5), but it is a call to reconciliation in all cases under the guidance of respected spiritual men and those of experience in the Church.

Would that when we differ with one another over material matters we resort to understanding and prayer and readiness to give up some rights for the sake of love. And if we do not agree, let us return to the Church in the person of its fathers and guides, so that they may decide between us in these material matters, which are less important than the spiritual matters in which they guide us; and thus we keep our love for one another. Let us put love and peace above the love of material things.

entries.section: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

paragraphs.text: It is a fault in you that there are lawsuits among you over the matters of this worldly life. Why do you not prefer to bear wrong and not seek to resort to the courts? Material loss is nothing beside the loss of brotherly love.

entries.section: (1) The prohibition against resorting to pagan courts

paragraphs.text: He rebukes them for wronging one another, which leads the wronged to resort to the civil courts, whereas Christian principles urge them to love the brethren as members in one body and in the fellowship of the one Church.

Would that we imitate Christ, who suffered for us: "who, when He was reviled, reviled not again; when He suffered, He threatened not; but committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously" (1 Pet 2:23).

entries.section: (2) The sins that deprive one of the Kingdom

paragraphs.text: "Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?" There is no doubt that you knew that whoever wrongs others has no inheritance in the Kingdom of Heaven. And know that the vices mentioned next prevent entry into the Kingdom, because most of those who were around them, of the pagans, committed them without any reproach of conscience. These vices are: fornication, idolatry, prostitution, and falling into sexual perversion ("effeminate": those who lie with males), theft, covetousness, drunkenness, reviling and extortion, that is, taking what they have no right to. And to show them how their condition changed when they became Christians, Paul reminded them that they used to practice those vices before in their pagan society, but now he says to them: you are completely separated from the former evils, for you have been purified and washed in the sacrament of Baptism and consecrated to Christ in the Myron, and you were reckoned righteous by what Christ did for you and by the work of the Holy Spirit in you.

Always remember your new, pure nature which you received in Baptism, so that you keep away from sin and do not share in it with the people of the world. And do not forget that you are consecrated to God in your heart, your senses and your thoughts, so that you remember His word and seek Him in all His gifts and in the events that pass over you.

entries.section: (3) Do not be enslaved to the demands of the flesh

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul raises us to a new spiritual degree, so that we refrain not only from evil but also from things that are permitted, eating of them only what agrees with and suits our life in God. Just as a person understands that for every occasion he wears the clothing suited to it, so many things do not suit the spiritual man although they are not sins in themselves and may be used in special cases, such as drinking wine, which was used anciently as a medicine in some cases, or the stripping of solitary ascetics, who wear few clothes, but this nakedness does not suit ordinary life.
And more than this, a person must not be attached to any material thing so that it comes to dominate him, whether food or drink or anything material.

entries.section: (3) Do not be enslaved to the demands of the flesh

paragraphs.text: The belly was created in man to receive food, and God created both for man's benefit and bodily need and to obtain strength to fulfill his obligations toward God and society. But this arrangement is temporary for life on earth and ends with the end of his temporal life, for in eternity there is no eating or drinking. It is true that the belly is for foods and foods for the belly, but a person must not be a slave to his belly, and likewise the body must not be for fornication, because God did not create the body of man to commit fornication; the body belongs to the Lord, and Christ bought us with His blood. The pagans thought, as some wicked people like them also say now, that fornication is a natural need of man. Of course this is evil, and God did not create the body for fornication, that is, for bodily relations outside marriage.

entries.section: (3) Do not be enslaved to the demands of the flesh

paragraphs.text: God cares for the body, and since He rose as the firstfruits of them that slept, He honored His body, which is like our bodies, and He will raise them glorified at the second coming. So it is not permissible for a person to defile his body by fornication.

entries.section: (4) Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: You know that the bodies of believers are members of the body of Christ, which is the Church, for they partake of His most holy Body and Blood, so they are His and are His members. Is it fitting, then, for any believer among us to take the members of Christ and make them members of a harlot? Paul utterly rejects this by saying, "God forbid."

entries.section: (4) Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: A man's union with his wife makes the two one flesh, as the Scripture says: "A man shall leave his father and mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh" (Gen 2:24). So he who is joined to a harlot becomes one body with the harlot, and the two become partners in one defiled and hateful life, which does not befit one who has become a member of Christ, for by this he separates himself from membership in the Church.

entries.section: (4) Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: But he that is joined unto the Lord becomes one spirit with Him, that is, he is filled with the Spirit of God, who is the Holy Spirit, and walks in complete obedience to Him and refrains from everything that is contrary to this glorious union. This is why God forbade fornication, because it is not a sphere of love and holy unity, but a sphere in which each party exploits the other to satisfy his lusts.

entries.section: (4) Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: Refrain completely from everything that can lead to committing the sin of fornication. All the sins of the heart, such as hatred, envy, reviling, lying and others, do not defile the body of the one who commits them, but fornication corrupts the body as well as corrupting the spirit, because the fornicator uses his body contrary to God's purpose in creating the body, in addition to his corrupting the physical, mental and moral powers of man, and it is often the cause of serious diseases.

entries.section: (4) Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: As I made clear to you before and you know well, your bodies are Christ's and the dwelling of the Holy Spirit which God gives you, so they are for God and not for man.

entries.section: (4) Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: For Christ redeemed you and bought you with His precious blood, and this great price with which God was pleased to redeem man is proof of the value of the human soul to God.

So glorify God for your redemption and for the greatness of the price with which you were bought, by dedicating your bodies as temples for the indwelling of the Holy Spirit and by keeping them pure, and by keeping your spirits in the love of God and obedience to Him, for it is the breath of life whose source is God, as the Scripture says: "And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Gen 2:7).

Let us reflect on our persons, spirit and body, to know that they are a trust deposited with us which we will return to their Owner, who is God, so we have no right to defile them. And let us guard our senses, which are the entrance of sin, so that our bodies remain pure, and let us fill them with spiritual things, such as looking at the icons of the saints, repeating the prayers, and hearing spiritual words along with reading the Holy Bible.
Marriage and virginity

entries.section: (1) The lawfulness of both marriage and virginity

paragraphs.text: "Now concerning the things whereof ye wrote unto me", which is understood to mean that they were questions about marriage and not marrying: I would say to you that it is good for a man not to marry, if he is able, because virginity is a person's consecration of himself to the love of God.

entries.section: (1) The lawfulness of both marriage and virginity

paragraphs.text: If a man is unable to control his natural inclinations and to raise them to a higher level, let him marry, so that every man has his own wife only and every woman her own husband only.

It may seem from the above that marriage, as the Apostle indicates here, is merely a safeguard against falling into fornication, and that there is therefore something of a lowering of its dignity in this. But the matter is not so, because the Apostle himself spoke elsewhere of the lofty moral side of marriage and regarded it with honor and holiness (as in v. 14, ch. 11:3, Eph 5:25-27); the safeguard is one aspect of marriage in the view of St. Paul, and not all its aspects.

If you are married, do not forget that your goal, like that of the virgin, is the love of God. Give sufficient time every day to your prayers and your meditations on the Holy Bible. Moreover, use marriage as an opportunity to come out of your preoccupation with yourself and to offer love to the one with you, so that you rid yourself of the obstacles to the sense of God and always grow toward your goal.

entries.section: (2) The marital relationship

paragraphs.text: The husband must feel the wife's due from him, which consists of tenderness and love; likewise the wife must render to the husband his due, which is esteem and faithfulness. This is recalled during the Prayer of the Crowning according to our beautiful Church rite, when the priest hands the bride to her bridegroom and says in the exhortation: You must, O blessed son, receive your wife in this blessed hour, and strive for what is for her good, and be tender toward her, and hasten to what pleases her heart. Likewise he says to the bride: And you, O blessed daughter... you must honor him and revere him and not go against his opinion... and meet him with cheerfulness and welcome, and not lose any of his rights over you, and fear God in all your affairs with him.

entries.section: (2) The marital relationship

paragraphs.text: The husband and his wife become one flesh in the sacrament of marriage, so neither of them has power over his own body, but the other has it; therefore it is not the right of either to refuse the marital relationship because of lack of inclination for it, because his body belongs to the other. How then can he prevent the other from acting freely in what the other owns?

entries.section: (2) The marital relationship

paragraphs.text: So I advise you that none of you withhold the marital relationship from the other, except with the consent of the other party to this abstaining, and for a certain period, so that they may devote themselves to fasting and prayer, and then the marital relationship is resumed, so that neither party is exposed to the temptation of Satan, who tries to make you fall into sin because of your inability to control your natural inclinations.

entries.section: (2) The marital relationship

paragraphs.text: I say this meaning abstinence. It is necessary within marriage, as a declaration that the goal of marriage is love and the enjoyment of the presence of God between the spouses, and not a constant indulgence in bodily passions; so we enjoy this relationship but only for a time, and then return to our only goal in life, which is the love of God. And he says it by way of permission and not command, meaning that there is freedom in determining the periods of abstinence within marriage according to the need of each of the spouses and under the guidance of the father of confession.
There is another opinion, that his saying this refers to marriage as a whole, so it is by way of permission to whoever wishes and not a command, and whoever can live in virginity, that is better.

How beautiful is love within the sacrament of marriage, which makes each party forget his own desires and seek the comfort of the other, and this is so in all the matters of life. So care for the desires of those around you before your own desires, that you may rejoice in the smile on their faces and your heart be glad.

entries.section: (3) Celibacy does not suit everyone

paragraphs.text: "For I would that all men were even as I myself", unmarried, that is, celibate; and yet I bear in mind that every person has his own abilities. One has a gift to live as I do without marriage, and another has the gift to marry.

entries.section: (3) Celibacy does not suit everyone

paragraphs.text: I say to the unmarried, or those who were married but have become widowed, that it is good for them if they continue thus without marriage, as I live celibate.

entries.section: (3) Celibacy does not suit everyone

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless, this approval of celibacy does not rise to the rank of a command; if these cannot control their natural inclinations while abstaining from marriage, let them marry, for it is better for a person to marry than to labor in resisting his natural inclinations.

If you are not able to attain complete bodily virginity, do not be troubled, but strive toward spiritual virginity, that is, that Christ be the Bridegroom of your soul, and that you take care to please Him in everything before pleasing yourself or others.

entries.section: (4) No divorce

paragraphs.text: The phrase "I command, yet not I, but the Lord" does not mean that the previous opinions are personal opinions of the Apostle Paul, but means that what is to come was already spoken by the Lord in His Gospel (Mt 5:32). The Lord Jesus commanded that the woman not be separated from her husband, when He was on earth before His ascension into heaven, as recorded in the Gospels (Mk 10:9, Lk 16:18); that is, He commanded the stability of the marital relationship and forbade divorce except for fornication. So the people of Corinth, to whom the Apostle Paul writes, no longer needed teaching on this matter because they had the teachings of the Lord Christ.

entries.section: (4) No divorce

paragraphs.text: If it happens that the wife departs from her husband for any other reason, let her remain thus without marrying another, and if she cannot live alone, let her seek reconciliation with him. And what I say of the wife I say of the husband also: he must not try to leave his wife. Thus in cases of marital disputes, reconciliation is the solution, and even in cases of fornication, if the other party forgives the party who committed fornication, they can be reconciled and live together. And from the teachings of the Lord Christ, to whom be glory, and the Apostle Paul's reminder of it, the Church does not allow divorce except on the ground of fornication. Our Church still holds to this law which the Lord of glory laid down to this day, and does not approve any divorce except for the ground mentioned.

When differences of opinion and problems occur between spouses, it is not right to quarrel or for either party to leave the house, lest the dispute increase and others intervene, and the distance grow and thoughts of separation and divorce by illegitimate ways begin. Let us give a chance to love, understanding and forbearance, and let each look to the virtues of the other and to the importance of preserving the structure of the family and not disturbing the children.

entries.section: (5) Mixed marriage

paragraphs.text: In the apostolic age, when a married pagan believed and his pagan wife did not believe, but she did not wish to leave her bond with her husband, let him keep her; and the reverse also: if the woman believed and her pagan husband was willing to remain with her, let her live with him in a normal married life.

entries.section: (5) Mixed marriage

paragraphs.text: The unbelieving party, when living with the other who believed, learns from him the Christian virtues, that is, is sanctified in him; and likewise the children learn from the Christian father or Christian mother spiritual conduct and become clean and pure.

entries.section: (5) Mixed marriage

paragraphs.text: "Under bondage": compelled to live with the pagan, because the pagan refuses to stay with the party who has become a Christian.

The believer may live with the unbeliever if the latter consents. But if the unbeliever wishes to separate from him, let the Christian party leave him, because he will not benefit from living with him, since the pagan is insistent on his conduct and his life, and there is no strong love binding him to the Christian party so that he would imitate his conduct and learn from him.

entries.section: (5) Mixed marriage

paragraphs.text: If it is possible for both parties, the believer and the unbeliever, to live in peace, the believer must not separate from the unbeliever, because in their life together there may be a favorable opportunity for the believer to save the unbeliever and draw him to the faith.

This permission which the Apostle Paul gave to the believers at the beginning of the spread of the faith was granted in special circumstances that existed then, but it is not for application at the present time, after the spread of the faith; the Church does not allow the marriage of a believer to an unbeliever, in accordance with the saying of the Scripture: "Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers" (2 Cor 6:14). And this shows us the depth of the marriage bond.

The bond between the members of one family makes them influenced by one another's conduct. So pay attention to your behavior and your words, carrying out the commandments of Christ, so that you save your soul and be an example to those with you; and even if they oppose you or mock you at times, be confident that your good conduct has an effect on them. Do not be negligent or despair, and pray for them.

entries.section: (6) On circumcision and slavery

paragraphs.text: The Apostle makes clear the unimportance of the first condition in which a person was before the faith. Whether he was a circumcised Jew or an uncircumcised Gentile, what matters is that he walk as a Christian after his faith, and not try to change his bodily state by having the Gentile circumcised, because the proof of faith is keeping the commandments of God, as the Council of Jerusalem declared that the Gentiles who believed in Christianity had no need of circumcision (Acts 15:1-19, Gal 5:2).

entries.section: (6) On circumcision and slavery

paragraphs.text: Likewise the social condition of the pagan before the faith does not matter. If he was a slave, he is not asked as a believer to leave his master, but if he can become free, let him seize this opportunity (at that time a slave could buy his freedom by doing extra work for which he received pay and placing it in the temple of one of the gods until a sum equal to the price of his freedom was gathered, and then his master went to the temple and received this sum from the hand of the priest, and the slave became free).

entries.section: (6) On circumcision and slavery

paragraphs.text: "Freeman": that is, free in the Lord.

He who was called to the faith while he was a slave has in truth become free with a spiritual freedom, and the person who is free in his social standing must realize that true freedom is in submission to Christ. For true freedom, in both cases, is not outward freedom, but the freedom of the spirit from sin and its submission to God in holy worship.

entries.section: (6) On circumcision and slavery

paragraphs.text: Whether you are slaves or free in your social standing, you are slaves of Christ who bought you and paid a costly price for you, His most holy blood; so in all your conditions, slaves or free, you belong to Christ, so do not submit to the conduct of the wicked and become enslaved to them by imitating their sins.

entries.section: (6) On circumcision and slavery

paragraphs.text: Let each one remain in the condition in which he was when he accepted the faith, but let him take care to be always near to God and to live in a way that pleases God. In general, Christianity's remedy for social problems goes to the depth of the problem and not to its outward symptoms.

Do not be troubled by any deficiencies or weaknesses in you, for God completes them and supports you, so that your spiritual life or your service is not hindered, for God is able to work with the little and the weak so that you thank Him and glorify His holy name.

entries.section: (7) Work for eternity

paragraphs.text: "Now concerning virgins" who are not married, I have no direct commandment from the Lord. For the Lord Christ, when He spoke about marriage and divorce, did not go on to speak about virgins; but I give my opinion as one chosen by the Lord and entrusted with the teaching, and I write a holy book under the guidance of the Holy Spirit to carry out the task of teaching. For because of the troubles and afflictions to which we are exposed in our present time, it is good for a person, whether a man or a virgin, to remain thus without marriage.

entries.section: (7) Work for eternity

paragraphs.text: If you are bound to a wife, do not seek to leave her; and if you have not yet married, or were previously married and then separated from her for valid reasons, such as your pagan wife's separating from you, do not marry.

entries.section: (7) Work for eternity

paragraphs.text: If you cannot control yourself in not marrying, it is no fault of yours if you marry. So also for the virgin: she does not sin in anything if she marries, if remaining as she is, a virgin, is beyond her capacities. But in general what I advise you is out of compassion for you, for the troubles and hardships you may encounter in connection with the persecutions which the Christians were undergoing at that time, since the married will meet more affliction. So the talk is about the circumstances of persecution in the apostolic age and not about virginity in general.

entries.section: (7) Work for eternity

paragraphs.text: I say this to you, brethren: the time we live on earth is very short compared with eternity. So I advise you not to be occupied more than is fitting with our passing life, but with our spiritual duties which qualify you for eternity, so that the marriage bond with its responsibilities may not occupy you so that you give it all your time and all your heart, and it distracts you from your spiritual duty.

entries.section: (7) Work for eternity

paragraphs.text: Do not let the sorrows or joys of the world occupy you either, for worldly joy, however great or large, is temporary joy, and likewise the sorrows of the world will one day end. Also, the possessions of this world or the greatness of position and authority must not distract you from the goal of your striving and struggle, which is the enjoyment of the eternal glories.

entries.section: (7) Work for eternity

paragraphs.text: Those who possess much of the goods of this world must not yield to its enticements nor surrender themselves to its passions and pleasures. For all the things of this world, its appearances and its glories, soon end and pass away, so they do not deserve that we cling to them at the expense of eternity, which must be cared for in the first place.

Remember every day that it may be the last day of your life, so that you repent and prepare for eternity and live with Christ through your ordinary life, that is, so that your aim in your home, your work and all your relationships is to know God and show Him to others.

entries.section: (8) The superiority of virginity

paragraphs.text: I would have you not be absorbed in the many responsibilities of marriage, because the unmarried can devote all his concern to what pleases the Lord, since the demands of married life do not occupy him.

entries.section: (8) The superiority of virginity

paragraphs.text: But the married man has less concern for God, because he is occupied with worldly concerns which consume a large part of his time in order to provide the family needs for living in this world, and which please his wife.

entries.section: (8) The superiority of virginity

paragraphs.text: The difference between the married woman and the virgin is that the unmarried woman can give all her time and effort to what pleases the Lord, being consecrated to Him in body and spirit because she is not bound by responsibilities which marriage imposes on her. But the married woman's married life requires that she turn to caring for what pleases her husband in all that he needs of her.

entries.section: (8) The superiority of virginity

paragraphs.text: Wahqan: a weight.

What I say in praise of not marrying and in speaking of the virtues of virginity, I do not intend to burden you, nor to oblige you to remain unmarried, which may be beyond your strength. I prefer that we live a life far from worldly entanglements and material preoccupations that can distract you from your spiritual worship, whether you are married or unmarried.
Would that we care for the things above, not the things on earth, always seeking what suits our eternity.

entries.section: (9) The opinion on marriage while enjoying the life of virginity

paragraphs.text: This discourse is addressed to some believers who marry on the condition of abstaining from sexual intercourse in order to enjoy the life of virginity. He says to them: if the man does not behave toward the one who lives with him as toward a virgin, but as toward his wife, that is, if he feels the necessity of living with her as husband because of their inability to control themselves, let him do so; he does not sin.

entries.section: (9) The opinion on marriage while enjoying the life of virginity

paragraphs.text: He who has resolved with certainty in his heart, without compulsion, and has power and authority over his own will, to keep virginity for his wife, does well.

entries.section: (9) The opinion on marriage while enjoying the life of virginity

paragraphs.text: The man who lives with his wife does well and does not sin in this. But the man who remains a virgin with his wife according to their common desire and without compulsion does better. Thus the Church teaches us in our spiritual striving that there is a good state, but there is a better state. So let whoever can receive the better receive it; but each according to the gift he has been given and the spiritual stature he has reached.

entries.section: (10) The dissolution of the marriage bond by the death of one of the parties

paragraphs.text: The married woman is bound to her husband according to the law of Christ as long as her husband lives, but if her husband dies she is free to marry whom she will, provided that the husband is united with her in the faith, so that her marriage to him accords with the will of the Lord.

entries.section: (10) The dissolution of the marriage bond by the death of one of the parties

paragraphs.text: But in my opinion she will be happier if she remains without a second marriage. I do not speak from myself, for the Spirit of the Lord who dwells in me guides me and gives me what to say so that I do not err. He permits marriage after widowhood, but prefers not marrying after widowhood as a kind of chastity, for the first marriage is enough, and he lives the rest of his life occupied with God, abstaining from bodily relations and the concerns of marriage.

Everything in the world God created for you; use it with freedom, but do not forget your goal, which is the love of God, and as far as you can, be content with the least possible of worldly attachments in food, drink, clothing and marital relations, so that you may give more time to your life with God and your service to Him. Eating what was sacrificed to idols

entries.section: (1) The superiority of love over knowledge
