paragraphs.text: Here our teacher the Apostle Paul speaks about the problem of Christians being exposed to eating the meat of the sacrifices that were offered to idols and then sold in the markets and eaten, whether in homes or in temples. He says to the Corinthians that we all know as believers that in truth there is no idol, and therefore eating what is sacrificed to them and sold in the markets does not affect us at all. But there are among us simple brethren who do not have this knowledge, and this conduct on your part may cause them to stumble. Our feeling that we know and others do not know may lead us to pride and superiority over others, and knowledge alone may harm, but if it is joined to love it becomes beneficial.

entries.section: (1) The superiority of love over knowledge

paragraphs.text: Here the Apostle Paul carries us to the thought of humility and states a truth that must be clear to everyone: that our knowledge, however much it increases and grows, is nothing but a drop in the sea, as the scholars themselves say; indeed it is incomplete knowledge. And he who is puffed up with his knowledge shows that he is lacking in knowledge, since he is proud although his knowledge is not complete.

entries.section: (1) The superiority of love over knowledge

paragraphs.text: Love is necessary for the knowledge of God, and the mind alone does not give us true knowledge about God, who knows and delights in the one who loves Him and teaches him by His Holy Spirit.
Would that we not rely on our knowledge as much as we rely on our prayer to God to illumine our way, lest we be puffed up.

entries.section: (2) There is only one God

paragraphs.text: As for the permitting or forbidding of what is sacrificed to idols, this depends on the question: "What is an idol?" And the answer is that it is nothing. The wooden, stone or bronze statues have no life and no authority over the affairs of men, and there is no living, true God except God.

entries.section: (2) There is only one God

paragraphs.text: What the pagans call gods, and they have thousands of them, in heaven such as the sun and the other heavenly bodies, or on earth such as trees and animals, does not affect the faith of Christians. And even if there exist beings superior to man in power and wisdom, such as the angels and the demons, which were called gods in the Old Testament, "For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords" (Deut 10:17), they too are creatures created by God.

entries.section: (2) There is only one God

paragraphs.text: But to us Christians, unlike the pagans with their many gods and lords, there is one God, almighty, the Father, the origin and source of all creation, and we love Him and live for Him; and we have one Lord, Jesus Christ, the Creator of all things.

If our God is the Creator and Ruler of everything in the world, then let our hearts be at ease and not be disturbed by the changes of life and the offenses or threats of others, for our God is able to fight for us. Let us rejoice in His company every day.

entries.section: (3) Eating what is sacrificed to idols

paragraphs.text: There are some Christians of Jewish origin who know that the idol is unclean and yet eat of what was sacrificed to it, and so become defiled, or Christians of Gentile origin who still think that the idol has power beside Christ their God, so when they eat of what was sacrificed to it they too become defiled. These the Apostle calls weak in their spiritual knowledge, that is, they do not know that the idol is worthless, so their eating what was sacrificed to it is counted uncleanness. But those who are perfect in knowledge, who know that the idol is worth nothing, their eating what was sacrificed to idols is counted as eating ordinary meat which God created, so it is clean food for them.

entries.section: (3) Eating what is sacrificed to idols

paragraphs.text: But food does not commend us to God, as the pagans believe that eating what is sacrificed to their idols commends them to their gods. We do not increase in our relationship with God if we eat of what was sacrificed to idols, nor do we lack if we do not eat of it, because it is merely ordinary meat and has no relation to our spiritual worship.

This saying is not against fasting. Fasting is a training of the will and not an abstaining from foods because of their uncleanness, since we believe that all foods are blessed by God, but we give up meat as a stripping of our material desires so as to be occupied with the worship of God.

entries.section: (3) Eating what is sacrificed to idols

paragraphs.text: You have a right, O strong ones, to eat of those sacrifices, but take heed lest this eating of yours become a stumbling block to your weak brethren whose consciences forbid eating of these sacrifices.

entries.section: (3) Eating what is sacrificed to idols

paragraphs.text: O strong brother, who are certain that the idol is nothing and that eating what is sacrificed to idols is like eating any other meat: but if a weak brother sees you eating at a feast held in an idol's temple (as was the custom of the people then, who reclined on couches before the table), he may conclude that you do this in honor of the idol, so he ventures to eat also, imitating you, and in his conscience he eats in honor of the idol, which destroys his soul, though Christ died for him.

entries.section: (3) Eating what is sacrificed to idols

paragraphs.text: By this conduct, O strong ones, you sin against the weak, because you push them to violate their consciences by eating meat that is unclean in their eyes because it was sacrificed to idols. And so you sin against Christ by causing the weak to stumble.

entries.section: (3) Eating what is sacrificed to idols

paragraphs.text: Therefore, although eating what is offered to an idol is not evil for the believer, who realizes that there is no idol, it is counted evil if it is the cause of others' stumbling; hence, if any food causes my brother to fall into sin, I will refrain from eating of it, lest I be the cause of his stumbling. For as a Christian I am responsible not only for myself but for my brethren also.

You must be careful in your conduct and actions so that you do not cause those around you to stumble, even if you intend no evil. But have compassion on those around you as Christ has compassion on you, and do not appear in ways that cause others to stumble.
The needs of the servant and his flexibility

entries.section: (1) Paul's apostleship and the cost of his living

paragraphs.text: Some of the Corinthians doubted Paul's apostleship and could therefore reject his teachings. Here the Apostle Paul affirms his apostleship with proofs, and puts forward several questions which are in fact a statement of the truth, that he is an apostle of the Lord Jesus. The aim of the Apostle Paul in his question "Am I not an apostle?" is to affirm that he is an apostle, and he proves this in the rest of verse 1 and in verses 2 and 3. As for his second question, "Am I not free?", he means that since he is a free man, he has the full apostolic rights like the rest of the Apostles, which include taking support from the Church, as will come later. Then the Apostle presents the first proof, which is that he saw the Lord Jesus and received from Him personally his apostolic ministry, and the second proof is their faith, which is the fruit of his preaching work among them.

entries.section: (1) Paul's apostleship and the cost of his living

paragraphs.text: "Others": those who came to Corinth after Paul left it and did not experience his apostleship, and so doubted it.

The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. If I am not an apostle to others, yet to you I am an apostle, and your faith in the Lord Jesus is sufficient proof of the truth of my apostleship, and so you yourselves are the guarantee and confirmation of that. The seal is the sufficient guarantee that the goods sent from one party to another are genuine.

entries.section: (1) Paul's apostleship and the cost of his living

paragraphs.text: This is the proof of the truth of my claim, and what I answer in my own defense to those who investigate the truth of my mission.

entries.section: (1) Paul's apostleship and the cost of his living

paragraphs.text: Have we not the right to live at the expense of the churches that we founded and served in, based on the word of Christ: "And into whatsoever house ye enter... in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire" (Lk 10:7)?

entries.section: (1) Paul's apostleship and the cost of his living

paragraphs.text: "Cephas": that is, Peter.

Have we not the right to go about preaching with a believing sister as a wife, whose support is also from the Church, like the rest of the married Apostles, who went about preaching with their wives accompanying them to serve their husbands and to preach to the women, and likewise "the brethren of the Lord", that is, the sons of His aunt, who are James, Joses, Simon and Judas (Mt 13:55), who also went about preaching with their wives?

entries.section: (1) Paul's apostleship and the cost of his living

paragraphs.text: Or do only I and Barnabas have no right to this, and must we work to provide for our living needs?

Know your rights so that you use them for the glory of God. It is not wrong to claim them, but take care not to lose your peace and clash with others, for your right to peace is more important than material rights.

entries.section: (2) The laborer is worthy of his hire

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul affirms the Church's obligation to meet the cost of his living, and gives three examples that illustrate the answer. The first is the soldier: he says that one cannot expect the soldier, while he fights in defense of his country, to support himself; the second is the vinedresser: he says that the vinedresser feeds himself from the produce of his vineyard; and the third example is the shepherd, who lives on the milk of his flock or its price.

entries.section: (2) The laborer is worthy of his hire

paragraphs.text: I do not say this according to my human opinion, but the Law, which is the law of God by the mouth of Moses, establishes that the preacher may live at the expense of the Church, for it is written in the Law not to muzzle the ox as it treads out the grain, to keep it from eating of what it threshes (Deut 25:4). Does God care for oxen more than He cares for man? God's purpose in this commandment is to establish a general principle, "the labourer is worthy of his hire", that is, the benefit of the workers among people. He who plows the ground or threshes the grain has hope of being rewarded for his labor, and the reward for work encourages diligence in it.

entries.section: (2) The laborer is worthy of his hire

paragraphs.text: If we have preached to you the word of God, which is able to lead you to eternal life, it is not much for us to take from you our material needs for this temporal life.

entries.section: (2) The laborer is worthy of his hire

paragraphs.text: The Christians of Corinth were convinced that other teachers than Paul had the right to take support from them, and that it was unjust not to meet Paul's support, though he was the first to teach them the Gospel and open to them the door of faith. But the Apostle Paul tells them that he voluntarily gave up claiming what was his right, and even bore the pains of need and the toil of manual work, lest anyone think that he served the Gospel out of greed for worldly gain.
The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

entries.section: (2) The laborer is worthy of his hire

paragraphs.text: Do you not know that the Levites who perform the service of the temple and assist the priests live on the offerings of the people to it, as God commanded: "The tithe of the children of Israel, which they offer as an heave offering unto the Lord, I have given to the Levites to inherit" (Num 18:24-32); and those who offer the sacrifices on it, who are the priests, the sons of Aaron, take a portion of every sacrifice as God appointed (Num 18:8-24).

entries.section: (2) The laborer is worthy of his hire

paragraphs.text: So also, as God ordained concerning the ministers of religion in the Old Testament, the Lord Jesus Christ commanded concerning the ministers of religion in the New Testament that they take their support from the people to whom they preach, and not do material work to provide for their needs (Mt 10:10, Lk 10:7). Therefore the believer must care to provide for the needs of the clergy and the consecrated, that they may be free for their service without distraction.

Would that you care to reward everyone who labors in any work to help you, and give him his due in full, not only with money but with appreciation and encouragement; and know that everyone around you, great or small, needs you to express your love to him.

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: As for me, by my own choice I did not use my right as an apostle to obtain my living expenses, nor do I mean by what I now write to you to obtain this right which I voluntarily refused to enjoy; for I would rather die of poverty and hunger than change the principle which I took upon myself in the service of the Gospel and of which I boast, which is not to burden anyone.

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: Preaching is not the subject of Paul's boasting; rather, preaching without pay is the reason for his boasting, for that which a person is compelled to do cannot be a reason for boasting to him. Paul preached because the Lord Jesus commanded him to, and if he abandoned preaching his conscience would rebuke him and he would be exposed to the wrath of God for resisting the heavenly call.

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: If Paul's preaching were voluntary, he would have a claim to a reward. But if it is of necessity because it is a divine command, then he is a steward entrusted with what he must do for his master, and he is thereby bound to serve his lord without expecting a reward.

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: The Apostle asks: What then is my reward, since I received no pay in return for my preaching of the Gospel, and did not use the right which the Gospel gave him as an apostle?
The Apostle himself answers this question in the following verses, making clear that his aim is to win everyone for Christ.

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: Although I am free and am not a slave to anyone and no one has authority over me in anything, I have labored in the service of many as though I were a slave to them, in order to guide all to Christ.

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: "Them that are under the law": the Jewish proselytes, that is, the Gentiles who became Jews and held to and submitted to the Law.

I agreed with the Jews in their customs and traditions and in their manner of living, in what does not conflict with my Christian doctrine, so that I might win their love and they might believe my teachings and obtain salvation. The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: As for the Gentiles, that is, the pagans who do not have a written law like the Jews, I did not follow the law of the Jews, as though I were without law, although I hold to the law of Christ and His commandments, which are more perfect than the law of the Jews; and I dealt with the Gentiles by the natural law, which is the conscience in every person, and which is the voice of God that leads us to faith in Christ and His teachings.

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: "The weak": they are those mentioned earlier in this same epistle. They are believers, but they do not have full knowledge of the teachings of the Gospel, and they were hesitant between the permitted and the forbidden among foods, the keeping of feasts and the other Mosaic teachings of that kind.

The Apostle Paul says that he did not rebuke the weak for their doubts, but proceeded gradually with them in teaching with all wisdom and gentleness in order to remove these doubts from their hearts. In sum, he says that he accommodated every group in everything that agreed with its behavior that did not conflict with sound faith, so that he might lead all to Christ.

entries.section: (3) Service is a divine commission to win souls

paragraphs.text: I do all this for the sake of preaching the Gospel, that I may obtain the blessings of the service on earth and then the eternal reward.

Would that you feel for those around you and share their thoughts and their lives, to win their hearts. For every person needs someone to share with him, and by that you enjoy strong friendships and find it easy to understand them, indeed you are able to influence them and lead them to life with God.

entries.section: (4) Striving to the end

paragraphs.text: "Prize": reward and recognition.

You know from what you see in the public arenas that those who run in the race course each strive to win the prize, but only one wins it. That is, merely running on the course does not make the runner deserve the prize, but persevering in the running until he reaches the goal, and so receives the reward.

entries.section: (4) Striving to the end

paragraphs.text: The athlete in the race course had to eat, drink and sleep by rule, and abstain from rich foods and wine, and devote a large part of his time to training. All that was in order to obtain the prize appointed for the winner of the race, which was a material prize that perishes with time, or even with the perishing of the person. But he who strives spiritually receives the crown of righteousness that does not perish. Consequently the crown that does not perish is worth the effort more than the perishable crown.

entries.section: (4) Striving to the end

paragraphs.text: So you must imitate me, for I strive and run toward a clear goal before me, which is winning souls for Christ, and I am confident of attaining the goal. I do not strive in vain like one who boxes the air and benefits nothing, or like one who boxes his opponent and does not hit him, since his blow lands in the air.

entries.section: (4) Striving to the end

paragraphs.text: I master my bodily desires, which can lead me to laziness and luxury and the other passions that war against the soul; I do not allow my bodily desires to enslave me, but subject them to the leadership of the Spirit who works in me, so that after having preached to many I may not be rejected by God because of my negligence, as He said: "Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling" (Phil 2:12).

Would that you persevere in your spiritual striving every day, holding fast to your prayers and your readings however busy you are, and examining yourself every day to correct your mistakes, and not surrendering to sin because you have been accustomed to it for a long time or because circumstances encourage you to it; and in the session of confession each month you renew your vigor and continue your striving with zeal.
Watchfulness and eating what is sacrificed to idols

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: St. Paul means by “the fathers” the Israelites who went out with Moses from the land of Egypt. The cloud is the one that covered them and guided them as they moved through the wilderness of Sinai, and the sea is the Red Sea, which was divided into two halves and through the midst of which they crossed.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: The inspired Word counted their going down into the depths of the sea, and the cloud covering them, as being immersed under the water, that is, as being baptized; and because Moses was their leader in this crossing, this baptism was ascribed to him.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: All the children of Israel shared in eating the manna, a symbol of Holy Communion, which the Lord gave them miraculously from heaven; therefore it was called spiritual food.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: Likewise all of them shared in drinking the water of the rock that Moses caused to burst forth in the wilderness, and because this too happened miraculously, it was also called spiritual drink.

As for the rock following them, there is a Jewish tradition which says that the rock rolled along behind them wherever they went, with water coming out of it, or that a stream of water came out of it and followed them on their journey in the wilderness. The rock is a symbol of Christ, because He was a support to them, quenching their thirst and caring for them.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: In spite of the many gifts God had bestowed on them, all the adults among them, except Joshua and Caleb, angered the Lord by their misconduct, their disobedience and their worship of idols, so He caused them to die in the wilderness and they did not enter the Promised Land.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: God intended these events to be a lesson and a warning for us, besides being a punishment for the Israelites for their sins. Here St. Paul warns the believers of Corinth against committing sins like those that prevented the Israelites from entering the Promised Land, lest they be deprived of entering heaven.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: Our teacher St. Paul refers here to the incident mentioned in the Book of Numbers (Num 25:1-9), when the daughters of Moab invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to the idols, and then the people committed fornication with the daughters of Moab, so the Lord caused them to die by a plague that cut down 23,000 of them. (The Book of Numbers mentions that those who died were 24,000. There is no contradiction in this: in the Book of Numbers the total number of those who died is recorded, whereas in the Epistle to the Corinthians the number of those who died in a single day is recorded, while the plague continued for more than a day.)

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: The Apostle refers here to what happened to the people anciently when the serpents destroyed them as they murmured against the manna (Num 21:5, 6); the Lord sent serpents upon the people, and they bit them, and many of them died. So he warns the believers of Corinth not to tempt Christ as they did, by their murmuring, their disobedience and their seeking of worldly pleasures, and not to expose themselves to evil in order to see whether Christ will rescue them or not.

entries.section: (1) The rebellion of the children of God and their punishment

paragraphs.text: He refers here to the rebellion of Korah and his companions against Moses and their rejection of his authority over them (Num 16); the earth was split open and swallowed them up, and they perished from among the congregation. This is a warning to the Corinthians that if they presume upon God’s gentleness and patience and transgress His commandments, they bring spiritual destruction upon themselves.

If God has given you good things, it is natural that you should thank Him for them. Let your outlook be simple, so that you enjoy God’s gifts instead of being distressed by what you lack and murmuring against Him; rather, know that it is by God’s permission, for your benefit. You can ask Him to remove the affliction, and for His help and support.

entries.section: (2) A warning to avoid falling

paragraphs.text: Here is a warning to the believers of Corinth not to be excessively confident in themselves. Their living in a pagan environment exposes them to falling into the sins of the Gentiles, just as happened to the people of old, who, although the Lord had singled them out for special care, rebelled and disobeyed, and so fell into idolatry and fornication, and tempted the Lord and murmured against Him, and thus exposed themselves to the divine wrath.

entries.section: (2) A warning to avoid falling

paragraphs.text: This is the rule that the Corinthians had to learn from the history of the Israelites: that as long as a person is on earth he is liable to fall. So whoever thinks that he is steadfast in faith and godliness should take heed lest he fall into sin, for the one who relies on his own strength is more liable to fall than others.

entries.section: (2) A warning to avoid falling

paragraphs.text: The word temptation in Greek means a test or an examination; so what is meant by temptation is that it is a means of examining and testing the steadfastness of a person’s heart toward God.

What is meant by the phrase “such as is common to man” is that these temptations are within the capacity and ability of human beings, who pass through them successfully if they rely on divine grace; for God is faithful in His promises, and never allows us to be exposed to a temptation that is beyond our ability to bear, but gives us strength and ability to pass through it. The way of escape is the means of coming out of the temptation, of sensing God and of regaining inner peace, such as God sending a solution to the problem, or the support of another person, or spiritual benefit from the temptation, so that its weariness is lightened...

entries.section: (2) A warning to avoid falling

paragraphs.text: Paul addressed the Corinthians with the words “my dearly beloved” so that they might be certain that his advice to them came from love for them and concern for their salvation. Here he asks them to keep away from idolatry, from entering the temple of an idol, from eating at their feasts, and indeed from any participation with the pagans in their rites; otherwise they would deprive themselves of the Lord’s help, which would expose them to falling.

Be assured that all temptations are by God’s permission, as long as you love Him and walk in His way; and however great your weakness, He will support you to pass through the temptation successfully and benefit from it. However hard it may seem, His divine power will open for you a way of escape from it in a manner beyond your understanding. So thank God at all times for His wonderful works with you.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: The Apostle regarded them as wise men, able to see that his words accord with sound reason, and that his forbidding them to eat in the idol’s temple is not merely a desire to impose his apostolic authority upon them, but that there are logical reasons that they can easily understand if they think deeply.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: The word fellowship in Greek means union. It was called the cup of blessing because it contains the blood of Christ, which was shed on the wood of the Cross. By eating of the bread, which is the Body of Christ, we are united with Him; therefore by partaking of the Body and Blood we become members of the Body of Christ.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: Our partaking of the bread and the cup means a real union with Christ, for the one body, even though it has many members, remains one.

Here is an affirmation of the truth and doctrine of the change of the bread and wine into the Body and Blood of the Lord; otherwise they would not create fellowship and union among those who partake of them. Let us beware of contrary doctrines that make the change dependent only on the faith of those who partake, or that deny this change altogether.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: Here is a proof, from what was done in the Jewish worship in the temple, of what St. Paul had already established concerning partaking of the Body and Blood of Christ. When the Israelites offered sacrifices to die on their behalf, as the command of the Law required, they believed that they were one with these sacrifices. In this sense, then, they were partakers of the altar. The Jews also used to divide the sacrifice and eat it among themselves, and no one could enter the temple and share with those present in eating the sacrifice unless he acknowledged that he was a Jew, united with them, worshipping with them the one God.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: Whoever takes part in offering a sacrifice to idols, or eats of it believing that it is offered to the idol, declares his faith in, and his fellowship in, the worship of this idol. The worship of idols gladdens Satan because it draws people away from the true God; therefore whoever offers sacrifices to an idol is united and associated with the demons. And I do not want this fate for you, which would take you far from God.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: A person cannot be a partaker in a thing and its opposite, just as it is impossible for light to be united with darkness. You cannot partake of the Lord’s Supper in a way that pleases God and profits your souls while you go to the temple of the idol, which is Satan, and take part in its feasts. Eating of what is offered to Satan will stand as a barrier between you and union with the Lord. But whoever eats of what was sacrificed to idols, not to please them but as a gift from God, does no wrong, because he believes not in the idols but in God alone, while taking care not to cause the stumbling of any of those who understand that eating the meat is honoring the idol and worshipping it (ch. 8:4).

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: Jealousy belongs to the nature of a man if his wife betrays him and loves someone other than him. The books of the Old Testament spoke of the turning of the people of old to idolatry as spiritual adultery, and of Israel as the bride of the Lord. God expressed His anger as jealousy, as stated in (Deut 32:21 and Ps 78:
58.) The question here expresses astonishment at the folly of the Christians who provoke God’s wrath by attending pagan feasts.

Paul’s second question, “are we stronger than he?”, is a rhetorical question, for we are in no way stronger than the Lord. It is not permissible for Christians, who are the bride of Christ (Eph 5:25-31), to provoke the Lord’s jealousy by sharing in the table of demons.

As long as we partake of the Holy Sacraments, it is not fitting for us to attend parties that please Satan because of the dancing, drinking of wine, songs and arousing of desires in them, such as the parties held after the sacrament of marriage is completed in the church. How can we be united with God and Satan at the same time?

(4) Freedom and causing others to stumble (vv. 23-33, ch. 11:1:) 23 All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not. 24 Let no man seek his own, but every man another’s wealth. 25 Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience’ sake: 26 for the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof. 27 If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go, whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience’ sake. 28 But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience’ sake: for the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof: 29 conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another man’s conscience? 30 For if I by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that for which I give thanks? 31 Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God. 32 Give none offence, neither to the Jews, nor to the Greeks, nor to the church of God: 33 even as I please all men in all things, not seeking mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved.
Ch. 11:1 Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: This repeats what was previously explained in (ch. 6:12), that Christian freedom is not absolute. When we were united with Christ, our aim became to please Him and to keep away from evil, from whatever causes others to stumble, and from everything that is unprofitable or unedifying, such as excess in eating and drinking, or being in places that are not fitting for the children of God, or wearing clothes that draw attention; likewise any useless talk, or wasting time in fruitless occupations.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: The believer must prefer the benefit of others to his own personal pleasure, even if what he does is sound and pure but causes the weak to stumble; so he forgets his own comfort and mood and seeks the comfort of others.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: Whatever is sold in the meat markets, eat of it without asking whether it was sacrificed to an idol or not, because by this question you expose your consciences to stumbling and doubt.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: For the Lord God is the Creator of the earth and all that is in it of fruits and animals; all of it is God’s, and He has made it food for man, and there is no need for doubts and debate over whether to eat it or not.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: If you wish to accept an invitation from unbelievers to eat with them, and you are willing to accept their invitation, there is no objection to your eating what is set before you, on condition that you do not ask whether it is from the sacrifices of idols or not, so that you do not burden your consciences.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: But if one of those invited with you, one of the brethren weak in faith, tells you that this is sacrificed to an idol, because he imagines that it is forbidden, then if you eat you wound his conscience. So do not eat of it, out of regard for his weak conscience, even if you are convinced that it is clean because it is from the hand of God and your conscience did not rebuke you for eating it, because there is no reason to refrain from the food except to avoid causing the believing brother to stumble.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: I say this not for the sake of your own conscience; your conscience does not rebuke or condemn you if you eat of what was sacrificed to an idol, and you are not compelled by your conscience to refrain from eating it, but for the sake of the other, who imagined that eating of it is forbidden. Why should I expose myself to my brother’s blame, as though I were guilty for acting according to my freedom, and cause him to be weakened in his faith and to stumble? He has a right over me that I refrain from causing his conscience to stumble, just as I refrain from what makes my own conscience stumble.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: God has graciously given me the right to partake of this food, so I have the right to eat and give thanks; but this is not a sufficient reason for me to cause my brother to stumble by eating what he imagines it is not lawful for me to eat, that is, he considers that to be worship and fellowship with idols.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: This is a rule that every believer must observe in all his words and deeds, so that the purpose of all of them is the glory of God and not his own glory; for this is the chief end of man.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: Do not cause the Jews to stumble by anything in your dealings with idols, and do not cause the pagans to stumble by encouraging them in anything connected with pagan worship, but do everything that urges them to leave that worship. Likewise with regard to believers who are weak in faith, do not be a cause of their stumbling by your actions, even if those actions are permissible.

entries.section: (3) Fellowship with the Lord and fellowship with Satan

paragraphs.text: Before St. Paul asks anything of them, he reminds them that he himself behaves in this way, so that his words are more convincing and acceptable. He never sought to please himself, but did everything that does not conflict with his faith, while at the same time pleasing others, in order to win them to Christ so that they might be saved. Ch. 11:1: So be imitators of me in denying self, in avoiding the causes of stumbling, and in seeking the salvation of souls by every possible means; and I also imitate Christ in His conduct and His teachings, and in this St. Paul is a faithful guide to others.

May you be considerate of those around you, and neither say nor do anything that makes them stumble or distracts their minds from God. And you, my sister, take care about the clothes you wear to show your beauty and elegance, without troubling those around you. Let us all remember the value of these souls around us, for they are more precious than anything, since their price is the blood of Christ shed for them.
A woman covering her head and preparing for Communion

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: In the following verses the Apostle offers solutions to some of the problems that had arisen in the Church of Corinth. To lead them to obey his instructions, he begins his discourse by praising them as brethren of his who always remember him and keep all his teachings and the traditions that he delivered to them as he had received them from the Lord.

The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. The word “teachings” appears in the original Greek as the equivalent of the English Traditions, meaning customs handed down; therefore we ought to hold fast to the sound traditions that we have received from our spiritual fathers.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: Head: an origin or source.

The head of the man, that is, his source, is Christ, who created him; and the head of the woman is the man, because he is her origin, for she was created from one of his ribs, and therefore she is subject to him as the leader of the family.

As for the relationship of the Father and the Son, that is, Christ, the Father means the origin from whom the Son was begotten; and the Son, because He bears all humanity in His body, obeys the Father in order to bring all humanity into subjection in obedience to God.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: Every man who prays or preaches must not put a covering on his head, because his putting on a covering is an insult to Christ, who is the head of the man; it is as though he were trying to hide the glory and splendor of the image of God, whereas he ought to display this image. As for the priest, when he wears a turban it signifies dignity, and when he prays the Liturgy he covers his head with an ornamented white covering that symbolizes the splendor and glory of God, because he represents Christ in the Liturgy.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: A woman’s hair is a glory and an adornment to her, but before God she has no glory of her own, and she covers it in submission to Him. Here the Apostle says, in an ironic style, that when a woman uncovers her head she is like one who shaves her head, and this makes her appearance ugly.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: If a woman does not cover her head, she might as well cut her hair as a man cuts his. And if it is disgraceful for a woman to cut her hair, she should cover her head and not try to imitate the man in having his head uncovered, since a shaven head for a woman was a mark of shame in both Jewish and Roman society. The Apostle wants to say here that just as it is a shame for a woman to shave her head, so it is also a shame to her and to her husband for her not to cover her hair.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: Our teacher St. Paul instructs the man not to cover his head because he bears the image and glory of God; he is the origin of God’s creation, and he is the one whom God created to proclaim God’s authority over creation. But for the woman he instructed that she cover her head in the Church, as a declaration of her respect for the rule that the Lord established, which is that the man is the head of the woman and she is subject to him; she is thereby “the glory of the man,” or a good reputation to him.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: The man did not come from the woman at the beginning of creation, whereas the woman came from the man, because she is a rib from his ribs, flesh of his flesh and bone of his bones.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: In (Gen 2:18) the Lord God said, “It is not good that Adam should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” This means that Eve was created for Adam and not the reverse.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: For this reason a woman must cover her head, just as the angels cover their heads and faces with their wings before God as they praise Him.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: With the Lord there is no difference or distinction between man and woman except in the form that serves their unity and increases their bond with one another.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: Just as the woman was taken from the man, so also the man is born of the woman. And if Eve was taken from Adam’s body, this was accomplished by God’s creative power, for all creatures are from God.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: St. Paul put this question to the Corinthians, saying: Examine the matter among yourselves and answer. Is it fitting for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?! For by our nature as human beings we understand that it is a disgrace for a man to let his hair hang loose like women (with the exception of those consecrated in the Old Testament, who were not to cut their hair, or what some ascetics do in the New Testament, as a kind of indifference to the hair because the whole mind is occupied with God.) The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: The opposite is true for the woman, because a woman’s hair is an adornment and beauty to her and a splendid covering for her head; it is, as it were, a natural veil for her, and she should not boast of this adornment, that is, her hair, in the house of God.

entries.section: (1) The Apostle’s instructions concerning a woman’s head covering

paragraphs.text: If there is anyone among you who is not convinced by the foregoing proofs that require a woman to cover her head in church, and wishes to argue about this matter and create dissensions and strife, this is not our custom, for we walk with one heart and in obedience to the guidance of the Church.

May we sense God’s presence in prayer, and submit to Him with humility, whether the woman by covering her head or the man by submitting in his heart. Thus we are in repentance and contrition before Him so that we may obtain His mercies, and at the same time we thank Him and rejoice in being in His hands, whether the prayer is in the church or in the closet inside our homes.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: My instruction to you now is in fact not meant to praise you; it is painful that when you come together in the Church you do not come together for the better, that is, so that one may benefit the other and work for his spiritual edification, but so that one of you may reproach the other and harm him spiritually.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: I hear that when you come together in the Church there are divisions and schisms among you, and I believe part of what I have heard of these divisions. Such is the inclination of some toward factions and disputes over matters like eating what was sacrificed to idols, or marriage and virginity...

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: For the devil must needs fight you, and you, as human beings, are liable to fall into divisions.

God has allowed such deviations of thought to appear so that those who have approved love, and from whom such weaknesses do not proceed, may become manifest among you; for the badness of some reveals the virtues and holiness of others.
The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: When you gather in the Church for the prayer of the Liturgy and the partaking of the Mysteries while you are in this state of division, your selfishness and the weakness of your love toward one another appear, and your gathering loses its purpose, which is love.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: A table was connected with the prayer of the Liturgy, at which they ate together as a sharing of love in eating food with one another; but it seems that some of the rich would eat alone what they had brought, instead of sharing it with the poor, and so the poor man went hungry and the rich man was drunk from too much eating and drinking, because, such being the case, the poor man’s portion was nothing but the little that he had brought.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: Therefore the Apostle rebuked them, saying that it would be better for them to eat in their own houses whatever they pleased and not shame the poor, because by this they despise the idea of brotherly love, and so they need rebuke, not praise.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: Christ delivered to Paul, when he spent three years with him in the wilderness (Gal 2:17, 18), what He accomplished on Holy Thursday when He instituted the sacrament of Communion, which He delivered to them to practice as Christ’s commandment throughout the generations. “He took bread”: the word for bread in Greek is (artos), and this word is applied to leavened bread, not unleavened.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: After giving thanks, He broke the bread into pieces, and then said, Take, eat: this is My Body, which is offered as an offering for you on the Cross. And what I am doing now, you must do continually, so that you may remember the sacrifice of the Cross that I offer for your salvation.

And since this took place before the actual Cross, as St. Gregory the Theologian said: Christ crucified Himself for the world before the world crucified Him. That is, He had slain Himself by intention; therefore He gives His Body, broken by intention, which would be slain on the Cross on the morrow.

The word “remembrance,” as it appears in Greek, is Anamnesis, and it does not mean merely the remembrance of something absent, but rather the presence of that which we make the remembrance of. That is, the bread is changed into the true Body of Christ and is not merely a memorial of a historical event.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: In the same way Christ took the cup after He had finished supper, and said that this cup contains My Blood, which is the New Covenant, because the covenant was written and sealed with My Blood, and you must do this continually in order to remember Me and remember My holy sacrifice for you.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: Whenever you eat of My Body and drink of My Blood, you must proclaim My redemption and My salvation of all humanity until I come at My Second Coming.

And sharing in Communion places on the believers the responsibility of evangelizing and preaching in the name of the divine Christ, in a hymn that reminds us of our responsibility, all of us, the hymn “Amen, Amen, we proclaim Your death, O Lord.”

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: What confirms that the bread truly becomes the Body of Christ and the wine His Blood is this warning to which St. Paul points for whoever eats of the bread or drinks of the wine unworthily. If the matter were merely a symbol, it would not be attached to a warning and admonition of this kind.

The word worthiness means repentance and confession at the hand of the priest for everyone who approaches this sacrament. So with regard to what happened among the Corinthians, namely that whoever among them approached Communion while distinguishing himself from others by eating sumptuous food, approached unworthily and was like a criminal against the Body and Blood of the Lord, because he does not love or care for those around him, and so is not worthy to partake of the sacrifice of divine love, that is, the Body and Blood of Christ.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: Let a person examine his depths and offer repentance for every weakness or sin that he sees, and confess in the Church; then let him approach to eat of the holy bread, which is the Body of Christ, and to drink of the holy cup, which contains the Blood of Christ.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: But the person who eats and drinks without repenting exposes himself to punishment from the Lord because of the contempt he shows toward the bread and wine, as though he did not distinguish between the bread that is changed into the Body of the Lord and ordinary bread, and did not distinguish between the wine that is changed into the Blood of the Lord and ordinary wine. The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. All this confirms that the bread and wine in the sacrament of thanksgiving are not ordinary bread and wine but are changed into the Body and Blood of the Lord.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: Because many of you approach to share in the Lord’s table without repentance, they expose themselves to punishments from the Lord. Some of them suffer weakness, some suffer sickness, and some are punished with death.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: For if we examined ourselves in the fear of God, and stood before ourselves in the position of a judge to judge whether we are worthy to approach to share in the Lord’s table, and then amended our way of life by repentance and restored love in our hearts toward all, we would not be exposed to punishment.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: The Lord’s aim in punishing the unworthy, for their lack of the due preparation before approaching the Lord’s table, is to discipline them to repentance, so that they may not be condemned in eternity along with the people of the world.

entries.section: (2) Preparation for the sacrament of the Eucharist

paragraphs.text: Finally he instructs that the believers wait for one another in order to eat together, and that no one go ahead with eating his food before the others come; and if he is hungry, let him eat at home, because this table means the fellowship of love among the believers and not merely the satisfying of the appetite for food.

The remaining matters: details of worship and Christian conduct that the Apostle taught them when he visited them, and which belong to Holy Tradition, that is, the oral teachings that have come down to us and that we live out in our worship and our conduct.

Take care to examine yourself, to repent and to acknowledge your sins before the priest before Communion, so that you may become pure and worthy of the Holy Mysteries. Moreover, if any evil thought fights you during the Liturgy, repent of it before God until you meet your father of confession.
Spiritual gifts

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: St. Paul speaks in this chapter about spiritual gifts, beginning his discourse with the importance of acquiring the virtue of humility, and then the ability to distinguish between what is genuine and what is counterfeit of these gifts.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: I remind you of what you were before you accepted the faith, and how you were led away to the worship of idols that cannot speak. Therefore none of you has any merit in anything of the gifts he has obtained.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: “Jesus accursed” (anathema): that is, Jesus a criminal deserving the punishment of the Cross. This cannot come from a believing Christian, because Christ is God, who suffered for us to redeem us.

Whoever claims to have received spiritual gifts and at the same time denies Jesus is certainly a false pretender and not a true believer. Denial of Jesus was common among the Jews and the pagans, because the teachings of Jesus exposed their craftiness and the falseness of their idols. In this is a warning against unbelievers creeping in among them.
And no one can confess Jesus as Lord and God except by the grace given him by the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: Gifts are the free gifts that the Holy Spirit bestows; they are many and varied, but their source is one, the one Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: Likewise the ministries by which a person can serve the Church of God are many and varied, but they all serve the Lord Jesus.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: Likewise the works that glorify God are of many kinds, but God, who gives a person the ability and grace to carry them out, is one God; it is He who works in all, and He is the source of all gifts, and all of them share one aim, which is the salvation of man and the manifestation of God’s glory.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: The Holy Spirit makes known His work in every believer through the spiritual gifts He gives him for the benefit of the Church.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: Wisdom is the knowledge of God’s dispensation for the salvation of man, whereas knowledge is the interpretation of the prophecies and types of the Old Testament concerning Christ and salvation.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: To another is given strong faith, of the kind that can remove mountains, so that nothing is impossible for him.
And to others is given the gift of healing various diseases, so that they are treated and healed by the miraculous work of the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: Working of miracles: the Spirit gives some the ability to perform miracles, which are works above nature. Some are given the ability to prophesy, which is the proclamation of things that will happen in the future, or spiritual teaching; and the teachings that speak of preparation for the Kingdom, which is a future matter, count as prophecy. To others is given the ability to distinguish between true and false prophets. He also gives some the ability to speak in different tongues, while others receive the ability to interpret these tongues and make them understood by those who listen to them.

entries.section: (1) The Holy Spirit is the source and distributor of gifts

paragraphs.text: The important matter that the Apostle affirms here is that all these gifts, in their various kinds, are bestowed by the one Holy Spirit; He gives each believer according to what accords with God’s will, in a way that works for the edification of the Church and the benefit of all believers.

If God has given you a gift, do not be proud of it over others, because it is from the Holy Spirit and not from you, and if you do not humble yourself and use it well for the benefit of the Church, God can take it from you. And know that the gift does not save you, but is for the benefit of the Church, and you can benefit from it like the rest of the believers whom you serve with this gift, so that you receive the fruits of the Holy Spirit, that is, the virtues, and this is evidence of your sound spiritual conduct on the way to the Kingdom.

May you discover, with the guidance of your father of confession, what abilities God has given you so that you may serve the Church with them, and beware of being slack in showing these gifts or abilities; it is not right to bury God’s gifts, even under the pretext that you are unworthy of service. And these gifts are not only those mentioned above, but every ability to do any service is a gift from God.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: Our teacher St. Paul likens the Church, which is the Body of Christ, to the body, which, though composed of a great number of members, yet with the multitude of these members and the difference of their functions is one body, since all of them work in unity and harmony for the edification and growth of this body. This is an attempt by the Apostle to clarify the place of the different gifts in the Church and their relation to one another, and likewise the relation of the believers to one another.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: All believers form one spiritual body, because we were all baptized and born again in one Baptism by the Holy Spirit, and became members of the one Body of Christ, whether we were Jews or Gentiles, that is, in terms of nationality, or bond or free in terms of social standing. Whatever our former religious or social position, we have all been made to drink from one fountain, which is the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: The edification of the body is completed by its many members. The body cannot be only one member. Likewise the Church is many believers, and each member in it has his gift and ministry different from the other’s, but in the end, by their completing one another, they fulfill all the needs of the Church.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: If the foot should say, I am not the hand, and therefore I am lesser in rank as to my task when compared with the tasks of the hand, so I consider myself outside the body or separated from it, would it by saying this not be counted a member of the body?
So it is with you, O believer. If you have a certain gift and do not have some other gift, does that mean that you are not a member of the one body of the Church with the other members?

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: Is it possible for the ear to be separated from the body because it is not an eye?
So each member must sense the importance of his place in the Church, and that however small his work may be, it has an importance that the Church cannot do without.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: It is necessary that the one body have many members with different functions. For if the whole body were an eye, who would perform the function of hearing? Likewise if the whole body were hearing, and there were no member for smelling, who would perform the function of smelling?
So it is also with the Church: if all had the same gift, who would attend to the other needs of the Church? If all were teachers, who would clean the church or collect the offerings...?
Let us then cease from murmuring, and not look at what we do not have but at what we have, so that we may work with it without vain comparisons.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: God assigned to each member of the body its own task for the service of the whole body, and furnished it with everything it needs to carry out its task most fully. In this the wisdom of God appeared plainly, by placing each member in the place suited to it.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: If all the members of the body were one member, the body would lose its completeness, because the constitution of the body requires many different members with varied functions.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: There are many members of the body, and yet these many members form one body in which each member depends on the other members, but all of them work in perfect harmony for the good of the one body.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: No member of the body, however great its task for the body, can dispense with the task of any other member. For example, the eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of you, nor the head to the feet, I have no need of you.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: Rather, much more those members that seem to be weaker by their nature, such as the eye, for example, when compared with other strong members; for those members, in spite of their lack of endurance and their natural weakness, are ones that the body is in urgent need of.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: Those members which, according to their functions, are thought to be without honor, we surround with more abundant honor, and those members that it would be unseemly to have exposed we cover, because God gives them more beauty and importance than the rest of the members.
Here he is speaking of the reproductive organs, which are distinguished from the other members by sharing with God in His work, which is creation, when they bring forth a child.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: There are some members, such as the face and the hand, which by their nature have a beautiful appearance and do not need us to cover them with the intention of giving them better beauty.
But God made the body to consist of members that differ in honor and appearance, giving the weaker members, such as the reproductive organs, greater honor.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: God did this wisely in blending the different members together, so that there might be no room for division among the members of the one body, and so that each member might care for the other members and all have one concern, which is the benefit of the body as a whole.

entries.section: (2) Believers are members in the body of the Church

paragraphs.text: The existence of this strong unity among the members of the one body makes the whole body feel pain when one of the members is hurt, and if one member is honored, that is, if the head, for example, is crowned, all the members share in this honor; the eye laughs when the mouth speaks with joy.

May we feel for those around us, sharing their joys and sorrows by putting ourselves in their place, so that we can share with them in our hearts and our deeds, for we all need psychological support and encouragement so that we may pass in peace through the changes of life.

entries.section: (3) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: But you, each of you as a member in the Body of Christ, has his uniqueness and personality or gift, which was given to him by the Holy Spirit. Each of you is a part of the life of the Church as a whole.

entries.section: (3) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: As the members of the one body differ in their functions, so also believers differ in the gifts given to them. So God set in the Church people for the apostolic ministry, that is, the ministry of the Apostles and their successors the bishops and priests; then people for prophetic teaching, which leads to repentance and the salvation of souls, as it helps each believer to uncover his spiritual state; and after that teachers who have the ability to teach Christian doctrines and clarify the right understanding of them. He gave some the ability to work miracles and others to heal diseases, and gave others an aptitude for serving the orphans, the widows, the poor and others who need help and assistance, and others wisdom in managing the spiritual and material affairs of the Church, and to still others it was given to speak in different languages.
In sum, gifts are varied, and the Church is in need of all these gifts.

entries.section: (3) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: Is it logical that all the members of the Church should be apostles? And can they all be prophets or teachers? For there to be a teacher there must be, in turn, a learner. And is it natural that all should have the ability to perform miracles? Then they would not be miracles if everyone were able to perform them.

entries.section: (3) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: Likewise, is the ability to heal diseases given to all?
And if all speak with tongues, what is the benefit?
And likewise, if all had the ability to interpret tongues, for whom would they interpret if all had this ability?
The meaning of this is that God gave each one a particular gift, and in His wisdom did not will that all should have the same gift.

entries.section: (3) The kinds of gifts in the Church

paragraphs.text: If this is so, and if the Church is in need of these varied gifts, you should seek the gifts that are more profitable and useful for the Church. I show you a more excellent way by which you can acquire the better gifts, and that is love, as will appear in the next chapter.

Do not be occupied with the abilities you do not have; the gift is a grace for which you will be called to account, but be faithful in discovering your gifts and investing them for the glory of God, and do not be slow to help whoever needs you, and always think positively: if you notice a lack in the Church, how you can supply it, or in any person, how you can help him. Thus you do not fall into judging, and your way is to do good to all.
Love

entries.section: (1) Love and the gifts

paragraphs.text: If you have been given the gift of speaking in many of the languages of men, or even if we imagine that you know the language of angels, which of course no one will know until he reaches the Kingdom, without having love, no benefit is achieved and there will be no fruit from this gift; rather you are like hollow words empty of any effect, like loud sounds with no real work. It is love that gives benefit to the gifts.

entries.section: (1) Love and the gifts

paragraphs.text: If I am given the gifts of prophesying God’s purposes, and I know the hidden mysteries of God’s will, and if I obtain all the knowledge that it is within a person’s power to obtain, and if I have a high degree of strong faith that enables me to remove mountains, that is, to work powers and miracles... if I have all this but my heart is not full of love, I am nothing. The essential characteristic of the spiritual person is love, not knowledge or the various gifts.

entries.section: (1) Love and the gifts

paragraphs.text: If I am prepared to give all my goods to the poor and to give my body to the fire as a witness to the Lord, but these deeds do not proceed from love, then these sacrifices and offerings, although they may benefit others, bring me no benefit and do not achieve the salvation of my soul, because they may be done out of pride or out of embarrassment before others.

Examine your words, your thoughts and your deeds in your relationship with others: is it love that moves them, or your personal aims? And when you notice people’s faults and rebuke them, is it with compassion and love, or out of annoyance at their behavior? If you feel love, then act as you wish; and if you do not feel it, withdraw until you first set your heart right, because your works are not acceptable to God.

entries.section: (2) The characteristics of love

paragraphs.text: Suffereth long and is kind: when a person’s heart is filled with love for all, he is not hasty to anger, but is long-suffering with offenders and tender toward them until he brings them out of their troubles, and is patient with beginners until they learn wisdom and upright conduct.

Love envieth not: love does not feel bitterness and pain when others succeed and are happy; and this is logical, because if love drives us to make others happy, how can we be pained when good comes to them? The one who loves does not think of acquiring for himself what others have, or become vexed at their good things and success, but rejoices and wishes them still more.

Love vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up: love makes us respect others and honor them, so that we are not filled with conceit and do not exalt ourselves in relation to others, because we love them and so honor them more than we honor ourselves.

entries.section: (2) The characteristics of love

paragraphs.text: Love doth not behave itself unseemly: when the loving person is compelled to reprove something that another has done, he does so with complete calm and in courteous words; he has such sensitivity that he takes care not to hurt the feelings of others even when they have erred, because he sees the beauty in others, while for their shortcomings he finds excuses and tries to help them correct them with gentleness and love.

Seeketh not her own: love is the opposite of selfishness and makes a person think of the needs and interests of others before his own; and God, who is loving, pours out more abundant blessings and cares for the person who lays down his life for others. He does not care for himself, but God cares for him.

Is not easily provoked: love does not make its possessor flare up in anger so that he protests in a loud voice or raises his hands and curses, or goes on until it comes to fighting and sometimes killing. This is because the loving person does not look at others in a spirit of criticism, seeking to condemn them; on the contrary, love makes him not reckon to others their faults.
Thinketh no evil: that is, it is not quick to assume evil intent in others or to accuse them of it, and is content with caution, while finding an excuse for them if their falling into evil is proved.

entries.section: (2) The characteristics of love

paragraphs.text: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth: the world encourages many sins and counts them success and distinction, such as lying and obtaining more than one’s personal rights; but love does not rejoice in people’s evils, but wishes for their salvation and rejoices in their good works, that is, the truth that is in them, which is the work of God that helps them toward virtues and good works.

entries.section: (2) The characteristics of love

paragraphs.text: Love beareth all things: the loving person bears the shortcomings of others and their faults against him.

Believeth all things: the loving person does not easily believe any evil thing that may be said about others, but simply believes all that is good before him, with caution and prayer, until God reveals how to deal with others, so that he escapes any evil. The loving person does not open his ears to the words of slanderers who seek to devise plots. Likewise love believes all God’s promises and commandments, whatever the surrounding circumstances of life or the conduct of people far from God.
Hopeth all things: sincere love never knows despair, expecting the work of God with calm, stillness, patience and hope in Him.
Endureth all things: true love is patient; it does not hasten results, and its patience is not quickly exhausted. God, who sees your patience and long-suffering, will give you a just recompense.

Truly, how broad is the work of love and its manifestations! And how much I need to review my conduct in the light of this, so that I may know my standing with respect to the Christian love required of me.

entries.section: (3) Eternal love

paragraphs.text: God is love, and since God is eternal, without beginning or end, love is everlasting and does not pass away, not even after death, although many things become void and come to an end with the end of time, such as prophecies, which are the foretelling of future things; they will end with the completion of salvation in eternity, for they will have no existence then, since they will have been fulfilled. And tongues, that is, the many languages, which are a means of understanding among people during their temporal life, will have no existence in the heavenly glories, where the luminous, glorified bodies will converse by means other than the languages we know.
And all the knowledge that a person can acquire in his temporal life will be nothing before the truth that will be revealed to all.

entries.section: (3) Eternal love

paragraphs.text: What we attain now of knowledge, or prophesy by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, is only a small part of the mysteries of the divine truth.

entries.section: (3) Eternal love

paragraphs.text: When the sun of the other life rises on us with the perfect truth, we shall not need this partial knowledge, which is like a lamp that is not needed in the light of the sun.

entries.section: (3) Eternal love

paragraphs.text: The Apostle clarifies here what went before. Just as when a person becomes a man he does not behave in the same manner as when he was a child, whether in speech, in understanding or in thinking, so also in the eternal glory you will reach the perfection of knowledge with which all partial knowledge is done away.

entries.section: (3) Eternal love

paragraphs.text: This is another illustrative example. We are now in the body, seeing things as through a mirror, that is, we see the image of things and not their reality, so our vision is imperfect. For this reason much of what we know about God remains not entirely clear to us, as though it were a riddle. But in eternity we shall see the things themselves and not their image, that is, in complete clarity and directly.

entries.section: (3) Eternal love

paragraphs.text: All this change will take place in the other life. But now, while we are still on this earth, the Apostle instructs us to abide in faith, hope and love, for these are the three foundations of the spiritual life. Faith is our trust in eternal life with Christ, but in eternity we shall see and perceive what we lived by faith on earth, and there faith will have no role. Likewise hope will end when the hopes we lived by on earth are fulfilled for us in heaven.

Therefore the Apostle exalts the importance of love, for it will never pass away and is always in the heart, on earth and also in heaven; for God is love, and in eternity we do not reach the end of God’s love, but we reach the utmost degree in our comprehension of this love.

Examine yourself: is your love toward God growing in greater concern for your prayers and your readings? And your love for others, is it increasing in more self-giving and sacrifices? A natural living being must always grow. So think how you can show love to everyone around you.
Preaching and tongues

entries.section: (1) The gift of speaking in tongues and of prophesying

paragraphs.text: Walk in love, but I also instruct you to strive to acquire the spiritual gifts, especially prophesying, which is teaching others the spiritual truths and interpreting the word of God by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit. It is far better than desiring the gift of praying in tongues, which many of the Corinthians desired; this was not used in teaching but was a kind of personal spiritual devotion in the closet, which no one hears, and he understands what he prays, and under the influence of his submission to the Holy Spirit he speaks truths and mysteries.

Perhaps many desired to acquire it as though it were a high spiritual degree, although the gifts, as we have mentioned, are not evidence of a person’s salvation but are given for the benefit of the Church.
This teaches us not to covet the gifts of others, but to invest what God has given us for the service of others.

entries.section: (1) The gift of speaking in tongues and of prophesying

paragraphs.text: But he that prophesieth, that is, teaches others (since prophesying is speaking about the future, and our future in the New Testament is the Kingdom and all the teachings that speak of God’s reign over our hearts and our preparation for eternity), speaks to people in understandable words that help the spiritual edification of the hearers, encourages them to spiritual conduct by preaching, and gladdens them with spiritual consolations (comfort) so that they continue the struggle.

entries.section: (1) The gift of speaking in tongues and of prophesying

paragraphs.text: Whoever speaks in a tongue in his closet edifies himself as a result of his sense of the Holy Spirit’s working with him, but the benefit of this does not go beyond his own person.
By contrast, whoever prophesies helps the spiritual edification of others, and so benefits the members of the Church who hear him.

entries.section: (1) The gift of speaking in tongues and of prophesying

paragraphs.text: I wish your desires to speak in tongues in prayer to be fulfilled, but I would rather that you seek after the gift of prophesying, because it is greater than the gift of speaking in a tongue in terms of its benefit to the believers; unless it is speaking in one of the known languages of the world, on condition that there is an interpreter so that the hearers may understand, because this language is known in other parts of the world, whereas the hearers need translation in order to understand and benefit spiritually.
