entries.section: (1) The gift of speaking in tongues and of prophesying

paragraphs.text: Now the Apostle takes himself as an example: if he came to them speaking in a language foreign to them, they would not benefit at all; but if he spoke to them in a language they understand, he would declare the truths of the faith that were revealed to him, and also all the spiritual sciences, and they would benefit greatly.

It is good that you enjoy prayer and delight in reading the word of God for your benefit. But you also need to be concerned to draw others to God and to teach them in the way suitable for them, so that they may be bound to the Church.
Be concerned for the repentance of those around you and for their partaking of the Holy Mysteries.

entries.section: (2) Speaking in tongues and interpretation

paragraphs.text: Here the Apostle brings an eloquent example that brings his thought near to the reader of the Epistle. He speaks of things without reason, that is, lifeless things, namely musical instruments that give out sounds, such as the pipe or the harp; if their notes do not give a melody that has meaning, with variety and effect, no one will listen to them, since they will give no benefit to the hearers.

entries.section: (2) Speaking in tongues and interpretation

paragraphs.text: The trumpet was used in wars in ancient times as a means of preparing for battle and conveying the commander’s instructions to the soldiers by means of agreed sounds. If the trumpet gave an unclear sound that was not agreed upon, the fighters would not know the commander’s instructions, and this unclear sound would have no useful role in the battle.

entries.section: (2) Speaking in tongues and interpretation

paragraphs.text: So it is with you also: if the language in which you speak is not understood by the hearers, they will not know what you mean, and your speech will be of no benefit to them, as though you were speaking into the air.

entries.section: (2) Speaking in tongues and interpretation

paragraphs.text: There are a great number of languages in the world, and the words in each have their meaning, but none of them will be of any use to me unless I understand that language; and I will not benefit at all from listening to a speaker whose language I do not know, and he likewise will understand nothing if I speak to him in a language that he does not know.

entries.section: (2) Speaking in tongues and interpretation

paragraphs.text: You also, since you strive earnestly to obtain spiritual gifts, ask that there be increased to you what is useful and good for the edification of others in the Church.

entries.section: (2) Speaking in tongues and interpretation

paragraphs.text: For whoever speaks in a language that the hearers do not understand will not benefit the Church in anything unless it is interpreted so as to become understood.

Therefore whoever receives the gift of speaking in tongues should ask God to prepare someone to interpret what he says for the benefit of the hearers, whether the interpreter is the speaker himself or another person; for this is a gift given so that he may speak with it when he goes to preach in a place where they understand only this language. But among his brethren who do not understand this foreign language, an interpreter is required, and otherwise let him keep silent, as the rest of this chapter affirms.

Be concerned to speak words suited to whoever hears you, not only simplified for the simple and for children, but suited to the nature, work and interests of the hearers, so that they come to hear you with eagerness and you are able to show them Christ through your speech.

entries.section: (3) Praying and preaching with understanding

paragraphs.text: It is not only that if I address people in a language they do not understand it does not benefit them, but also if I pray in a language other than my own and not understood, I feel the refreshing of the spirit, but I do not understand with my mind what I say, and my mind does not take part in the prayer.

entries.section: (3) Praying and preaching with understanding

paragraphs.text: St. Paul asks what is the duty toward the Holy Spirit’s gift to me of speaking in a tongue. He answers, saying that he must interpret what he says in this foreign language, and if he does not know how to interpret, let another interpret, one of those who have received the gift of interpretation. Likewise also when he chants in a language foreign to the hearers, he must understand with his mind what he chants, to enjoy the prayer and chanting more; otherwise there is no need to pray or chant in a foreign language that he can interpret neither for himself nor for others.

entries.section: (3) Praying and preaching with understanding

paragraphs.text: Otherwise the unlearned, that is, the one who does not know the language, who hears me when I pray in a language not interpreted for him, does not know when to say Amen when I give thanks to God, because he does not understand me, and there is no participation in the prayer.

entries.section: (3) Praying and preaching with understanding

paragraphs.text: You give thanks to God, and that is good, but the other, who understands nothing of what you pray, what benefit has he from your prayer? He gains nothing from it.

entries.section: (3) Praying and preaching with understanding

paragraphs.text: I thank my God that I speak with more tongues than any of you, but when I am in the Church I would rather speak five words that I can make understood by others, so that I teach them, than speak many words in a language that no one understands.

entries.section: (3) Praying and preaching with understanding

paragraphs.text: Therefore I instruct you to be like children in simplicity and innocence, but do not behave as if you were children in your thinking, unable to think seriously and deeply. That is, the Apostle wishes to stress the importance of understanding and perceiving spiritual things, and that the ability to build up the Church spiritually be the chief aim, and that speaking in a tongue not be the aim.
Truly, let us distinguish in our life between what is essential and what is additional.

If you are a servant, may you take care, when you lead others in prayer or chanting or when preaching, that it be in a way that encourages those present to take part, and that you not go alone in prayer and chanting at a speed that others cannot keep up with, or in tunes that most of those with you cannot manage; for the life of the Church is founded on fellowship among the believers.

entries.section: (4) The superiority of prophesying

paragraphs.text: The Apostle quoted the saying that appears in (Isa 28:11, 12), when He told His people who refused to hear His voice that He would punish them by sending them a foreign nation whose language they did not know, the Assyrian and Babylonian nation, and yet they did not hear. The Apostle's purpose in quoting this verse is to show that the use of foreign languages does not make, and did not make, unbelievers believers or the disobedient obedient.

entries.section: (4) The superiority of prophesying

paragraphs.text: Foreign tongues are given as a sign for the ministry of preaching among unbelievers so that they may believe when they see it as a miracle, as happened on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2:1-15); they were amazed, then were convinced and believed when each of them understood what was said in his own language. As for believers, the better thing for them is the word of prophecy, which is the interpretation of the word of God and religious teaching by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit in the language of the hearers.

entries.section: (4) The superiority of prophesying

paragraphs.text: If the believers come together in the Church and all of them are speaking with tongues, and there come in unlearned persons, that is, believers who do not know these languages, or unbelievers, they will judge of them that they are raving or that they are mad.

entries.section: (4) The superiority of prophesying

paragraphs.text: But if there come into the Church those who do not know the languages, or Jews or pagans, merely to look on at new things, and they find one speaking who preaches and teaches and calls to repentance, his words will affect them and prick their hearts, for the speech will be like a judgment upon them, and prove to them that they are sinners and liable to eternal perdition.

entries.section: (4) The superiority of prophesying

paragraphs.text: Thus he is exposed before himself as guilty before God and devoid of all righteousness, and he falls down before God as a sign of his repentance and bears witness to the truth that he has believed, and that you are the children of God, led by the Holy Spirit who dwells in you.

May you be occupied with the salvation of the souls of others and not with showing your own abilities, so that your concern may be like that of your Master Jesus Christ; and do not be afraid to show the truth even if it pricks some hearts, taking care not to fall into judging, and let the firm speech be with gentleness and meekness.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: What ought to be done when you come together for the worship of God in the Church is to take care to direct your gifts to the edification of the souls of the hearers.

“Hath a psalm”: that is, the Holy Spirit inspires him to sing a psalm, chanting and praising with it to the glory of God. In this is an indication of the origin of the prayer of the Psalms and the use of the Agpeya.
“Hath a doctrine”: that is, he has the gift of teaching one of the doctrines.

“Hath a tongue”: that is, the Holy Spirit grants him to speak in a new language for preaching; another has a revelation from the Holy Spirit to prophesy about the future or to disclose one of the hidden mysteries; another has the gift of interpreting languages. So let all your work be for edification and the repentance of straying souls.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: If anyone speaks in a foreign tongue, order is important in the use of this gift. The number of those speaking in a tongue must not exceed two or three at the most, and they must not speak at the same time but each in his turn, provided there is someone to interpret.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: If there is no one to interpret, let no one speak in a foreign tongue inside the Church, but he may pray in it to God alone.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: If there are prophets, that is, preachers, in the Church, not more than two or three should speak, each in his turn.
“The other”: that is, those who have the gift of discerning sound preaching from what is wrong or unprofitable; these must judge and direct those who have the gift of prophesying or teaching.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: If the Holy Spirit guides someone to add or to teach a spiritual teaching, the first must keep silent so that the other can declare these words. Thus worship proceeds in order and arrangement, and two do not speak at the same time.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: In sum, you can arrange the preaching one after another so that the hearers may benefit.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: Here St. Paul affirms the preacher’s ability to speak when he wishes and to be silent when he wishes, so that each gives the other the opportunity without crowding or disturbance. The prophets who preach to the people have a will that controls their spirits and their speech; they are silent when they wish or speak according to need, and their spirits do not rob them of their will so that they find themselves launching into speech in spite of themselves; rather they are able to control themselves.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: God, the giver of the gifts of prophecy, is a God of order and rejects chaos and disturbance. Accordingly order and peace must prevail in all the Christian churches everywhere, and each one must not crowd to show his gift, for this hides pride in the heart.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: The Apostle holds that it is shameful for a woman to speak in the Church. By this limitation of the woman’s authority, the Apostle defined the functions that none but a man may exercise in the Church. The Church, for example, restricts some of its spiritual functions to men and not women, such as the priesthood, and the priest is a teacher.

This does not mean the superiority of man over woman in kind or creation, but we must not ignore that there are natural differences between man and woman that have an effect in defining the sphere of activity and work of each of them, as stated in the Book of Genesis concerning the woman’s subjection to the man (Gen 3:16). But a woman can teach women and children. The preceding discussion concerns speaking and teaching in the Church that gathers men and women, whether in the Liturgies or in general meetings.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: A statement containing a rebuke of the Church of Corinth, because it seems they had departed from the orders of worship in the Church, so he wanted to alert them to the necessity of observing the Church’s order, which was established in accordance with the divine will. He asks them, with a kind of irony, whether your setting up strange orders in worship is due to your thinking that you are the origin of the preaching of the Gospel, or whether the right to arrange the worship of the Church belongs to you alone?!

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: If anyone reckons himself a prophet or that he has received spiritual gifts, let him know that what I instruct you is from the Lord. For Paul, as an Apostle, has authority from God to establish an order of worship in the Church, and a person cannot be a Christian called by God and have true spiritual gifts and yet refuse to hear His apostle and obey him.

This is a lesson for us. If a teacher claims to be sent by God and that we must obey him, we must compare his teaching with the teaching of the Holy Bible, and if it does not agree with it, we are certain that he is not from God.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: If anyone wishes to ignore what I instruct you, let him bear the responsibility for this ignoring. In this he clears his responsibility as an apostle who instructed them by the Spirit, while the responsibility of acceptance and obedience rests on them alone; that is, whoever obeys, obeys, and whoever does not obey is rejecting God’s teachings and will be judged.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: All the discourse of this chapter is about the two gifts mentioned, namely prophesying, that is, preaching, and speaking in tongues. This verse is the summary, which is that the first is better than the second and a Christian ought to desire it and be diligent in seeking it, and that the use of the second in the Church must not be prevented, because it too is profitable, on condition that there is someone to interpret so that the hearers may benefit.

entries.section: (5) The regulation of the use of gifts

paragraphs.text: All matters of worship must be done with order and concord in all the churches, and everything must be within the bounds of decency and according to the order established for communal worship. It is not right for an individual or a local church to deviate from the rest of the individuals and churches.

Take care to obey the teachings of the Church and the guidance of your father of confession, and if you want to add anything in your service, let it be with the approval of those in charge, so that it does not conflict with the order of the Church. The more you humble yourself, the easier it is for you to obey and to concentrate on the salvation of your soul and the love of God.
A reply to the heresy of denying the resurrection of bodies

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: It appears that some people in the Church of Corinth had denied the resurrection, like the Sadducee Jews or the Greek philosophers.

“I declare unto you”: I am amazed at your unbelief, as though you had never before heard in my preaching to you of the essential doctrines, of which the most important is the teaching of the resurrection. And if you have believed in it and live in it, it saves you as long as you hold fast to it, unless your faith is theoretical and you do not apply it in your life.

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: I inform you, brethren, that the most important thing in the good news that I and you have believed is the death of Christ for our sins to redeem us, and that He was buried in the presence of His disciples and then rose on the third day, as the prophecies declared in the Old Testament.

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: In verses 5 to 8 St. Paul enumerates some of the appearances of Christ after His resurrection, in the order in which they occurred. He appeared to Peter, then to the twelve (“the twelve” became a name for the company of the disciples, according to the original number applied to them, regardless of their number in a given circumstance; for on the day of this appearance they were only ten, because Judas had perished and Thomas was not with them.)

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: Then He appeared to five hundred brethren; although the Gospels do not give a clear indication of this appearance, it was most probably the day He appeared to the disciples in Galilee, as He had said to them before His death, “But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee” (Mt 26:32), and as He said to the two women on the morning of His resurrection, “Go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me” (Mt 28:10). Most of these witnesses were still alive about thirty years after the appearance of Christianity, so that anyone who doubts could ask them, and some of them had fallen asleep. The Church uses the expression “falling asleep” to indicate that the bodies of Christians are resting in their graves, awaiting their resurrection on the last day.

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: After that He appeared to James, then to all the Apostles, which is the appearance mentioned in (Jn 20:26) or in (Acts 1:4).

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: Seven or eight years after the Ascension of Christ, He appeared to Paul, who was then on his way to Damascus (Acts 9:3, 4). St. Paul likened himself to one born out of due time, that is, an immature child born before its time, because of his sense of unworthiness of the grace that Christ showed him.
God appears in your life in many forms, whether in His generous gifts or through afflictions; may you hold fast to Him and not turn aside from Him as your one aim in all your steps.

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: For I am the least of the Apostles in the apostolic ministry, and am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God. The Apostle said this out of his great humility and his deep regret over what he did before his faith. This humility did not prevent him from declaring his apostolic authority and the obedience due to him, so that people would obey his teaching for the glory of Christ and for the establishing of the truths he proclaimed, as he said in (2 Cor 11:5, 12:11).

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: “I am what I am”: my strength is not from myself but from God.

This grace that was given to him was not in vain but gave him strength for preaching; he founded more churches than the rest of the Apostles and wrote more books of the Holy Bible than all of them; yet he does not attribute his success in the ministry to himself, but all of this was by the grace of God working in him.

entries.section: (1) The resurrection of Christ and His appearances

paragraphs.text: Whether it was I or the other Apostles, we preach the resurrection of Christ from the dead, which is the fundamental subject on which our preaching is built, and by your accepting the faith you have also believed in the resurrection.

The grace of God that worked in St. Paul is ready to work in you if you believe and hold fast to it with earnestness in prayers, and feel your weakness more than all, so that the glory may be to God, and give all your effort to show your seriousness and your concern for what you ask of God.

entries.section: (2) The result of not believing in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: If we have proved the truth of Christ’s resurrection by conclusive proofs in our preaching, how do some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead, that is, that man perishes at his death and there is no other life after death?

entries.section: (2) The result of not believing in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: Every objection to the general resurrection is an objection to the resurrection of Christ Himself. For if there is no resurrection of the dead, this means that Christ has not risen, whereas the resurrection of Christ is certain to all because He took our body and rose in it.

entries.section: (2) The result of not believing in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: If Christ has not truly risen, then our preaching, we the Apostles, is not true. For we have preached that Christ rose, and that He is now alive and able to save whoever believes in Him, and if Christ has not risen all that becomes in vain, because a dead man cannot save the living. The foundation of your faith in Christ is your faith in His resurrection and that He is now seated at the right hand of the Father in heaven. If He has not risen, the foundation of your faith is falsehood and illusion and of no avail.

entries.section: (2) The result of not believing in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: Thus we become liars and false pretenders, because we give false witness concerning God in saying that God raised Christ, and this could not have happened if your belief that the dead do not rise were true.

entries.section: (2) The result of not believing in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: For if the dead do not rise, this means in consequence that Christ has not risen, since He took a body like our body.

entries.section: (2) The result of not believing in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: Christ died on our behalf to pay the price of sin. If Christ has not risen, it means that the debt of sin has not yet been paid, because the wages of sin is death. But since He has risen, He has satisfied divine justice.

entries.section: (2) The result of not believing in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: As a result of the preceding verse, those who have died having faith and hope in Christ have perished, if there is no resurrection.

Remember every morning, with the prayer of Prime in the Agpeya, the resurrection of Christ, that it may give you strength for a new beginning, so that you put away the sins of the past and walk circumspectly, and enjoy a fellowship with Christ that fills your heart with joy however much sorrows surround you, and so gain the ability to break through difficulties and to succeed by His grace.

entries.section: (3) We have a hope in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: If our hope, through our faith in Christ, is directed only to this earthly life, how wretched we are. For Christ did not give His followers a promise of any glory in this world; rather He made clear that whoever follows Him will pass through tribulation and pain and be exposed to many persecutions, but He promised us a hope of an eternal inheritance in His Kingdom after the resurrection.

entries.section: (3) We have a hope in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: But Christ has truly risen from the dead, and this resurrection of His is the pledge of the resurrection of those who have fallen asleep in the hope of eternal glory.

“The firstfruits of them that slept”: although He is not the first to rise from the dead, since there were those whom Elijah and Elisha raised, and those He Himself raised, such as Lazarus, the daughter of Jairus and the son of the widow of Nain, yet He was distinguished from them in that He raised Himself, and likewise did not die a second time; besides this, He rose to raise us up in Himself, for He died, though without sin, on our behalf to redeem us.

entries.section: (3) We have a hope in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: If death entered the human race through the first Adam, who transgressed God’s commandment, so also through the second Adam, who is Christ, the resurrection from the dead is accomplished. Every son of Adam inherits death from him, and every son of Christ inherits eternal life from Him.

entries.section: (3) We have a hope in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: For as Adam bequeathed death to his descendants, so also by the believers’ union with Christ they shall live.
This makes clear the first condition of salvation, which is faith in Christ, His death and His resurrection.

entries.section: (3) We have a hope in the resurrection

paragraphs.text: “In his own order”: in the original Greek it came with the meaning of in succession or in turn, that is, each one in his turn. Christ rose first as the firstfruits, and after Him the believers will rise at the Second Coming to live the eternal glory. The turn of mankind comes on the Day of Judgment, and they are glorified with Christ.

The phrase “every man in his own order” also indicates that the reward after the resurrection is according to the labor of each one; there are degrees in the eternal glory, to urge us to exert more effort here for God so that we may have the eternal reward.

The hope of eternity fills your heart with joy at what God has prepared for you, so you endure the sufferings of the temporary life, for however hard or long they are, they will end. On the other hand, you feel a drive for spiritual striving in worship and service to obtain the great reward in heaven.
May you think five minutes every day about the eternity that awaits you.

entries.section: (4) God all in all

paragraphs.text: After the Second Coming of Christ and the general resurrection will come the end of the present world and the end of the dispensation of salvation. The delivering up of the kingdom is easy to understand if we compare Christ’s kingdom over the present world with His eternal Kingdom, when there will be no rule or authority for the devil; accordingly, the delivering up of the kingdom to God the Father means that Christ has completed what was required of Him, which is redemption, and delivered it to the Father who sent Him to accomplish this mission. The delivering up of the kingdom to the Father does not mean that the Son does not reign, because the Father and the Son are one in essence.

entries.section: (4) God all in all

paragraphs.text: For Christ, to Him be the glory, must reign with absolute dominion over all, which will be accomplished in eternity after the Second Coming, when all the demons and the wicked will be subjected under the feet of Christ and cast into eternal torment.

entries.section: (4) God all in all

paragraphs.text: Death is an enemy because it entered the world through sin and was a punishment for it. To do away with death, the causes that led to it must be abolished. This is what was accomplished by redemption: Christ abolished death by the resurrection after He abolished all the causes that led to death, which are due to the envy of the devil. That is, He defeated the devil and his forces with a final defeat, and thereby abolished the death that the devil caused.

entries.section: (4) God all in all

paragraphs.text: The Father put all things under the feet of Christ, to Him be the glory, but it is clear that God the Father is not included among those subjected to Christ, because it is He who subjected all things to the Son, so He is not included among the things that are subjected to the Son. This is a preparation for the following verse.

entries.section: (4) God all in all

paragraphs.text: “God all”: God in three hypostases.
“In all”: God will be in all the believers, united with them and reigning over their hearts forever.

What is meant by the Son’s subjection to His Father is the complete subjection of humanity, in the Son, to the Father. For the Son put on the body of man and died for mankind to remove all causes of disobedience and sin, and to lead all, in the body of His humanity, to obedience to His Father; so the Son presents to the Father a new, complete world, so that the one God in three hypostases may be reigning over all.

That is, the Son will be subject to the Father not hypostatically but in respect of His being man; for the hypostases are not subject to one another, but their works are all subject to one another in completeness, harmony and a preconceived divine dispensation). See Rev 11:15, Lk 1:33, Dan 7:14) concerning the eternity of Christ’s kingdom.

So we have one God in three hypostases. And thanks be to God through Christ Jesus our Lord, who obeyed and was content to be subject to death in order to complete our salvation, and who is one with His good Father and the Holy Spirit, forever and ever.

Your subjection to God and obedience to His commandments rescue you from the bondage of sin and the humiliation Satan inflicts on you, because when you submit to your tender God, He raises you by His love to the degree of sonship, gives you the enjoyment of His company, and even glorifies you with Him in heaven.
So ask yourself every day, when you examine yourself, to what extent have you submitted to God’s commandments?

entries.section: (5) The resurrection encourages spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: Many of the pagans used to witness the death of the martyrs and would believe and be baptized. Why would they do this if the dead do not rise?

Is not this behavior of theirs, in accepting death in imitation of the martyrs, a witness to the truth of the resurrection of the dead? There is another view in the interpretation of this verse, which is the appearance of a heresy in the first century that said that if a catechumen who was learning the faith died before being baptized, another could be baptized in his place; so Paul says to those who follow this heresy, why are they baptized for the catechumens who have died if the dead do not rise? Of course Paul does not approve of this heresy, but he uses their error to prove the resurrection of the dead.

There is a third view, which is that “the dead” refers to the sufferings and persecutions undergone by those who come to the faith: why would they accept Baptism and the endurance of death every day if there is no other life after this present life that is full of suffering?!

entries.section: (5) The resurrection encourages spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: Why do we the Apostles expose ourselves to dangers for the sake of preaching the Gospel, if we have no hope in the resurrection and in eternal life?!

entries.section: (5) The resurrection encourages spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: “By your rejoicing which I have”: my boasting is in your faith.
“In Christ Jesus”: by the grace and help of Christ.
“I die daily”: I am exposed to death during preaching and ministry.

Paul declares his joy and boasting in the faith of the Corinthians, and this drives him to greater service and exposure to suffering and death so that their faith may grow and increase, and the grace of Christ supports him in this.

entries.section: (5) The resurrection encourages spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: If I were like a man, with merely human motives, concerned only with this life and not believing in the resurrection and eternal life, what would be the benefit of all my facing of the many wars and the great resistance from the opponents of the preaching at Ephesus?

If there is no resurrection after death, then let our motto be the motto of those who do not believe in eternal life, which is: let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. That is, not believing in the resurrection would make the endurance of suffering in the ministry useless and would drive us to indulge in material lusts.

entries.section: (5) The resurrection encourages spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: Do not submit to the evil ideas of the world that encourage bad desires. The Apostle advises them to cut off their relations with their former pagan companions, lest by associating with them their good morals be corrupted.

entries.section: (5) The resurrection encourages spiritual striving

paragraphs.text: He guides them to be watchful in order to do all that is good and not expose themselves to committing sins, because there were people living in their midst who deny the resurrection and are ignorant of God’s power, justice and goodness. He alerts them by this in order to stir their shame at such mistaken beliefs.

The risen Christ conquered death to urge us to be strong and conquer every sin, and also not to yield to any obstacles that hinder us from doing good. So when you meet any problem, remember your risen Christ and ask His help and go forward without fear, and God will deliver you from all afflictions.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: St. Paul supposed that an objector asks these two questions, showing the impossibility of the bodies rising after their corruption and dissolution, and that even if these bodies rose they would not be suited to the immortal spiritual state in heaven.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: We conclude from the Apostle’s answer that most of the objection is built on an illusion, which is that the resurrection body is the very same as the present body with its instincts and organs. So he rebukes them, showing them their ignorance in rejecting a doctrine that God has shown to mankind in the world of plants. The seed cannot sprout stems, leaves and flowers unless it is placed in the earth and buried to die, so that the change from the form of the seed to the form of the plant may occur, although the seed and the plant have the same essence.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: The seed changes completely into the plant that comes out of it. You sow a grain of wheat and it sprouts a plant entirely different from the grain in form, but not different from it in essence; every seed yields fruit after its kind, as God said in the Book of Genesis (Gen 1:12).

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: To every seed God gives, as He willed, its own plant body, which distinguishes it from the other plants; and although all plant bodies share the same constituents, they are distinguished from one another in the particular form of each body.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: So also with the bodies of animals: although each is flesh and blood, they differ greatly from one another. The body of man is not the body of beasts, nor the body of fish, nor the body of birds. That is, God made the bodies of animals differ to suit the conditions in which the animal lives, whether on the earth, in the water or in the air. This shows us that our bodies in heaven will differ in form from our earthly bodies to suit our heavenly state, although they are the same essence as the earthly body, but changed so that it becomes spiritual and lives forever.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: The Apostle mentions the distinction between the heavenly bodies (the sun, the moon, the stars and the other planets) and the earthly bodies (plants and animals) as evidence of the distinction between man’s body in this present life and his body in the resurrection. The heavenly bodies differ from the earthly bodies in appearance and in the nature of their making, and likewise man’s material body on earth will differ from his spiritual body in heaven, which will be in great glory.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: The brightness of the sun differs from the brightness of the moon. And the stars differ among themselves in the power of their light and brilliance and in other properties of each. The difference is not only between beings different in their nature but also between those of the same nature. Although the stars have one general nature, they differ among themselves.
So it is with the risen bodies: the righteous will differ in glory, and likewise the wicked among themselves in the degrees of eternal torment.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: Thus the resurrection body excels our present body. Man’s body in earthly life is exposed to factors of dissolution and corruption when it is buried, but in the resurrection it becomes incorruptible, not subject to weakness, death and dissolution.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: When the body of the mortal is laid in the grave, everything it had of beauty, strength and majesty leaves it, but in the resurrection it is raised in the image of Christ, and is in the utmost beauty and perfection of strength, as the Apostle says in (Phil 3:21), “Who will change the form of our lowly body that it may be conformed to the body of His glory.” Nothing is weaker than the corpse of the dead, for it is unable to do anything or defend itself, but at the resurrection the mortal is raised in a power suited to the new immortal life, and is not subject to any weakness or weariness.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: Man has a body suited to his nature, and on earth he shares it with all other living beings, and he has an animal soul that contains the instincts (what is meant by the soul here is the vitality in the body that moves all its organs and ends at his death.) But in the resurrection he will have a spiritual body led by the spirit, suited to his glorified nature, and in heaven he shares it with the pure angels.
If you believe in the existence of the first man, you must believe in the existence of the second. When the body is raised from the dead it is changed into the spiritual body.

The natural body is led by the animal soul that results from the union of the spirit with the body, whereas the spiritual body is led by the spirit, because its body is without instincts. For the animal soul does not share with the body and the spirit in the resurrection, but dissolves as soon as a person dies and does not rise.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: The Lord God formed Adam of the dust of the ground (Gen 2:7), and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, that is, the spirit, and Adam became a living soul from the union of the body with the spirit.

And the last Adam, who is Christ, to Him be the glory, after His resurrection came to have a spiritual body and was called a quickening spirit, because He has the power to give life to others, and the Spirit leads Him after the resurrection without there being an animal soul; He is spirit and a spiritual body, and there is no animal soul that moves the material body with all its instincts.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: The order mentioned in this verse agrees with what we see in all the works of God. We sow the seed in the earth, and the fruit or the tree comes first below the ground and then above it; the imperfect precedes the perfect, our bodily birth precedes our spiritual birth, and earthly life precedes the heavenly.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: The first man, who is Adam, was earthy because his body was created from the earth and was suited to dwelling in it.

The second man: He is the incarnate Christ, and He is from heaven in respect of His divinity, as the Scripture says, “he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven” (Jn 3:13). St. Paul’s aim is to say that Adam is from the earth and it is evident that we are like him here; and Christ is from heaven and we shall be like Him there, that is, with spiritual bodies led by the spirit without animal instincts.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: As Adam’s body was of the dust of the earth and is marked by weakness and liability to decay and corruption, so also are the descendants of Adam, because our bodies are of dust like his. And as Christ was the one who came down from heaven, so the believers in Him, the baptized, who have become His sons, at the resurrection will be in the image of the body of His glory in heaven.

entries.section: (6) The resurrection body

paragraphs.text: As we inherited from Adam his weak nature, liable to sickness, pain and death, so by the resurrection our bodies will become like the glorified body of Christ.

It is fitting for us to benefit from the possibilities of our new life by Baptism, which qualifies us for a glorified, heavenly life after the resurrection and gives us the ability to triumph over the evil enemy in the present world, so that we walk in purity and love toward all, and use the world and are not enslaved to it.

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: The natural man is composed of the body (flesh and blood), the soul and the spirit. The body in its present state is liable to decay and corruption, and therefore cannot be immortal in heaven; the corruptible body cannot inherit the incorruptible Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: I reveal to you a truth that was unknown but which the Spirit of God has revealed to us, which is that the people who are alive at the Second Coming of Christ will not die, but all of us, whether we are among these or among those who have fallen asleep, will have our bodies changed and take on new characteristics suited to the life of immortality.

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: The time of the shout of the angels and the last trumpet at the Second Coming is the moment of the change, in which the bodies of the living will be changed into incorruptible bodies, and in which also the dead will rise with incorruptible bodies.

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: This change must take place, because this corruptible body must be transformed into incorruption, and the mortal must become immortal, with the characteristics of immortality and eternity.

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: When our bodies have risen possessing the characteristics of immortality and eternal life, and the body has been transformed from a corruptible body into one not subject to corruption, death will no longer have dominion over us, and there will be fulfilled what Isaiah foretold, “He will swallow up death forever” (Isa 25:8), and as Hosea foretold, “O death, where are thy plagues? O grave, where is thy sting?” (Hos 13:14).

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: A rhetorical question that the Apostle takes from the prophet Hosea, by which he wanted to say that the dominion of death and Hades has ended forever by the resurrection of Christ. He likened death to a poisonous stinger like the scorpion, whose sting is deadly like a plague. And he addressed the grave, or the dwelling of the dead, as though it were a cruel jailer who held sway over mankind through the ages but was finally broken and released its captives forever.

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: Sin is the weapon by which death gained dominion over us, for whoever has not sinned does not fear death. The Law exposes sin and helps a person to recognize it and to feel its deadly authority, as though it had been given power to put to death the person who commits it.

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: Finally the Apostle gives thanks to God, who gave us the victory and provided the means of obtaining it by the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead.

entries.section: (7) The eternal inheritance

paragraphs.text: On the basis of the preceding proofs of the truth of the resurrection, I ask you, beloved, not to give heed to the false teachers who wanted to lead you to deny that fundamental doctrine of the Christian faith, and be steadfast in the faith of the Gospel, and abound in works whose aim is the glorifying of the Lord at all times; for the Lord will not forget what the believer has done or endured in his service, and will recompense him with a glorious resurrection, immortal life and a heavenly reward.
If eternal glories await us, let this drive us to every good work, and let us seize the opportunity of life to do good and show mercy to everyone, so that we may have greater glory in heaven.
The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. The final instructions and greeting

entries.section: (1) The collection for the poor

paragraphs.text: The believers in the Church of Jerusalem were in need of help, so St. Paul instructs the Church of Corinth, as he had previously instructed the Church of Galatia, to gather contributions to supply the needs of the poor of Jerusalem.

entries.section: (1) The collection for the poor

paragraphs.text: St. Paul asks them that each of them who is able should be diligent to lay aside on the first day of the week, that is, Sunday, the amount his means allow, so that no time is lost in collecting when he comes to them.
This shows that giving took place on Sunday, the Lord’s Day, when they prayed the Liturgies.

entries.section: (1) The collection for the poor

paragraphs.text: When I come to you, choose from among those you trust representatives of yours to carry your gift, sent with letters from me to Jerusalem; and I am ready to accompany the representatives if what they have collected is large and needs greater care in delivering it.

The Church is one in every place, so do not withhold your feeling for your needy brethren in any church other than your own, but help as much as you can, not only with money but with all the help you are able to give. And care for the poor, because Christ called him His brother, so you offer love to Christ Himself when you help someone in need.

entries.section: (2) St. Paul’s itinerary to them

paragraphs.text: I will come to you after I pass through Macedonia, for I have decided to pass through it first.

entries.section: (2) St. Paul’s itinerary to them

paragraphs.text: According to some scholars, St. Paul wrote his Epistle to the Corinthians at the Passover of the year A.D. 57, which means that the winter the Apostle would spend in Corinth was the winter of A.D. 57-58.

entries.section: (2) St. Paul’s itinerary to them

paragraphs.text: St. Paul planned to visit Corinth so that it would not be a mere temporary passing through to another place; he wanted to stay with them a sufficient time and not be content with merely passing by them, perhaps because of the many problems that were among them. But here he puts the Lord’s will first because he knows that the Lord arranges his missionary journeys.
This is an example for us to put the Lord’s will before our own will, and to know that it is He who arranges all our affairs according to His will.
The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

entries.section: (2) St. Paul’s itinerary to them

paragraphs.text: But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost, which is the feast of the descent of the Holy Spirit and comes fifty days after the feast of the Resurrection.
From this we learn that he wrote this Epistle at Ephesus, and the time of its writing was before the day of Pentecost.

entries.section: (2) St. Paul’s itinerary to them

paragraphs.text: The Apostle refers to the success he had met with in preaching, and how his ministry brought great results and good fruits. Yet this success stirred up the wicked against him.

The presence of problems in the ministry does not lead to despair; rather it may be a sign that the ministry is effective and that Satan has been moved to oppose it. So let us continue in our striving and likewise in our spiritual life, and if we fall let us not be disturbed but resist the devil and he will flee from us, and in the end God prepares for us many blessings and crowns.

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: Timothy was in Macedonia at that time and was on his way, as the Apostle had ordered him, to Corinth at the arrival of this Epistle to its people. So the Apostle asked them to support him against the false teachers who stir up some people against him, because Timothy does the work that the Lord commanded, that is, preaching, as Paul does.

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: St. Paul instructed them not to despise him for his youth, that he might return to him in peace with his companions after completing the work for which he sent him.

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: In spite of Paul’s encouragements to Apollos, he did not wish to come now to Corinth, that is, up to the writing of this Epistle, but he promised to do so when he sees that the time is suitable. Perhaps this was to avoid the quarrels between the parties that had formed in Corinth, where one says, I am of Paul, and another, I am of Apollos. So he wanted to delay his visit until matters calm down and the quarrels disappear.

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: In this verse are four commands suited to the circumstances of the Church of Corinth:

The first: “Watch ye”: the Church must always watch so as to be alert to the attacks of the enemy of good, and be warned of the evils mentioned in this Epistle, which are factions, quarrels, misconduct, and false teachers.

The second: “Stand fast in the faith”: that is, to stand firm in the truth that they heard from him and accepted and confessed, and especially to hold fast to the doctrine of the resurrection, which some had denied.
The third: “Quit you like men”: that is, to be courageous in standing firm before the enemies of the truth, to refute the arguments of the Jewish scholars and the philosophers of the Gentiles.
The fourth: “Be strong”: to endure hardships and persecutions.

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: He asks them that love possess their hearts and be the foundation of all their conduct in their homes and their spiritual gatherings.

The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians. The need of the Church of Corinth for this advice is evident from what was reported of the news of quarrels and what happens among them even in partaking of the Lord’s Supper. St. Paul elaborated on the subject of love in chapter thirteen.

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: Achaia: the southern region of Greece.
The saints: that is, the believers.

The Apostle refers to the house of Stephanas, which was distinguished as a whole family that had consecrated itself to the Lord. By the word firstfruits he means that the house of Stephanas was the first of the families to show the life of true faith that bears fruit in service to others.

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: St. Paul instructs them to cooperate with these and with whoever serves with them and labors in the Lord’s vineyard.
We find a similar commandment in the Epistle to the Hebrews, where the Apostle says, “Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls” (Heb 13:17).

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: The coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus from Corinth to Ephesus, where the Apostle was, was a comfort to him because of his distance from the people of Corinth. They eased somewhat his longing and anxiety for them.

entries.section: (3) Instructions concerning some servants

paragraphs.text: The good news these men brought relieved the Apostle’s soul and filled his heart with reassurance, and he also expects that through this Epistle which the Apostle will send them, they too will feel peace of mind.
He then instructs them to honor these servants and recognize their worth.
May we honor those who serve us, so that their service to us may be with joy and we may benefit from it to the utmost, because by this we honor Christ, of whom they are an image.
And as we humble ourselves we learn more from them and receive more abundant blessings from God, so that the ministry grows and many souls find rest in Christ.

entries.section: (4) Peace and the closing greeting

paragraphs.text: Aquila and Priscilla: a man and his wife who believed at the hand of Paul in Corinth and served with him; their trade was the same as Paul’s, which was tentmaking, so he worked it with them to provide for his needs, and they accompanied him on his missionary journeys.

Christians are bound together by a spiritual bond, and by virtue of this bond they feel their unity in Christ and convey greetings of love to one another. This is what the Christians in Asia (present-day Turkey) did with the people of Corinth.
It appears from this verse that the house of Aquila and Priscilla was used as a church for the believers, since it was not easy to establish churches because of the many persecutions.

entries.section: (4) Peace and the closing greeting

paragraphs.text: All the brethren send their greetings.

“Greet ye one another with an holy kiss”: this same expression is proclaimed by the deacon to the congregation of worshippers in the Divine Liturgy, and this holy kiss embodies the love latent in the hearts of the believers for one another.
The First Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

entries.section: (4) Peace and the closing greeting

paragraphs.text: “The salutation of me Paul with mine own hand”: this means that he wrote this phrase with his own hand, although the weakness of his sight made him dictate his letters to another. This phrase also confirms that the Epistle is authentic and was written by St. Paul.

entries.section: (4) Peace and the closing greeting

paragraphs.text: The Apostle considered the love of Christ to be the most important quality that distinguishes the Christian, and judged that its absence is the greatest of sins, and he condemns whoever is not characterized by it.
Anathema: a Greek word meaning delivered up to destruction.
Maranatha: its meaning is, The Lord is coming.
Let us look for the coming of the Lord with longing, and beware of falling into sins.

entries.section: (4) Peace and the closing greeting

paragraphs.text: St. Paul asks that the grace of the Lord Jesus be with the Corinthians. This petition of the Apostle includes every temporal and eternal blessing.

entries.section: (4) Peace and the closing greeting

paragraphs.text: By saying to them “my love be with you all,” he wanted the Corinthians to be sure of the intensity of his love and sincerity toward them, although he was compelled to rebuke them for some of their deeds, because his love for them is in Christ Jesus. Thus it is his duty to alert them to everything that could turn them aside from His way. Amen: its meaning is, May God confirm what I have said in this Epistle. When the Church says this word, it means an acknowledgment of the truth of the teachings declared, and that these teachings are the subject of their faith and hope.

The best thing you can offer to others is your love, which appears not only in a material form but first in kind words and care for their feelings, so that they see Christ in you and are reassured, and recover their peace in the midst of the afflictions of life.
